entries.title: Lens Flare
entries.text:
Lens Flare

veiling flareghost flareanamorphic streakrainbow flareVeiling glareLight striking the lens

Lens flare in lens flare cinematography is stray light scattered by glass, coatings, and barrel walls, producing ghosts, streaks, or veiling glare instead of a clean image. The artifacts live in the taking optic, so they track the source angle and dim when a body occludes the lamp.

Volume

Create this Lens Flare

Narrative function

When a hard source sits near or inside the frame, the camera admits it cannot contain the light. Contrast falls.

A ghost of the iris repeats across the field. The sun, a hangar opening, or a bare practical becomes a force the glass is failing to image.

Use it when the observer is overwhelmed: encounter lights, headlights, a door onto daylight. The audience should feel the camera struggling to see, not a sticker riding the grade.

It is the wrong tool when no source can explain the artifact. If blocking the lamp does not change the flare, you have an overlay, not an optic.

How it works

Place a small, hard source (sun, HMI, bare bulb) just off axis or in frame. Uncoated or vintage glass scatters more.

A dirty or filtered front element veils the whole field. Spherical lenses print circular ghosts that take the iris shape when you stop down.

For composites, parent flare position and intensity to the source and cut it when something crosses the beam. Prompt the source, its angle to the glass, and whether the result is veiling, ghosts, or both.

When to use it

A rescue worker opens a hangar onto daylight. The frame whites and veils, then clears as her body blocks the sun.

Do not drop a rainbow streak on a night interior with no lamp in the lens.

Compared with similar shots

Anamorphic Flare is a horizontal streak from cylindrical anamorphic elements, not general scatter. Halation is a warm bloom on the emulsion around a highlight, not light bouncing inside the lens.

Light Leak is unfiltered light hitting film or sensor from a body gap, usually from the frame edge, not from a pictured source.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

HalationHighlights should bleed like film, not clip like video.

Film GrainThe image should feel developed, not rendered.

In film

Close Encounters of the Third Kind lets encounter lights overwhelm the viewing system. Star Trek (2009) lets bright practicals streak and veil the frame.

Alien lets industrial sources dirty the glass. The Revenant lets the sun strike the lens as weather, not as a logo.

Close Encounters of the Third Kind 1977Powerful encounter lights overwhelm the viewing system.

Star Trek 2009Bright practical sources create conspicuous streaks and veiling light.

Prompt it

Name the source and the glass, not a pack. Example: Lens flare across [Subject], the sun or a hard practical striking the front element, veiling contrast, ghost orbs tracking the source, source-linked not floating.

Use in Video Generator

A rescue worker opens a hangar door onto dazzling daylight. As the source enters the lens angle, a restrained flare and brief veiling glare wash across the image, then clear as she blocks it. Realistic source-linked behavior, no floating decorative rainbow effects.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a grade overlay or an anamorphic streak pack with no lamp. Tell: the flare does not move or dim when the source is blocked, and it ignores occlusions.

Fix: put a real source in or near frame and parent the artifact to it.

Questions

What is lens flare in film?

Stray light scattered inside the lens as ghosts, streaks, or veiling glare. It is failed image-forming light, not a separate drawing on top of the picture.

Lens flare vs anamorphic flare

Lens flare is any scatter in the optic. An anamorphic flare is a specific horizontal streak from cylindrical anamorphic elements, often with oval bokeh.

When should I use lens flare?

When a hard source is in or near the lens and the camera should struggle to see. Skip it when the lamp is absent and the streak would float.

How do I prompt lens flare for AI image or video?

Name the source, its angle to the glass, and the artifact type (veil, ghosts, streaks). Require the flare to track and occlude with the source.

entries.title: Anamorphic Flare
entries.text:
Anamorphic Flare

An anamorphic flare is a horizontal streak produced when a bright point hits the cylindrical elements of an anamorphic lens. It is a subset of lens flare, not a general haze, and it usually arrives with oval bokeh from the same squeeze.

Create this Anamorphic Flare

Narrative function

Night lamps and headlights write a bar across the frame because the front optic stretches one axis. The streak is cyan, blue, or magenta depending on coatings, and it stays level with the squeezed world.

Oval highlights in the background confirm the same glass. Use it when the night should be written on the taking lens: wet streets, neon, a car coming toward camera.

The streak is evidence of scope optics, not of brightness alone. It is the wrong tool in spherical coverage, or when you want a circular ghost of the iris.

If the bokeh is round and the streak is a random rainbow, you have mixed two lens families.

How it works

Shoot anamorphic (typically 2x squeeze). Put a hard point source in or near frame: headlight, practical, sun.

Keep the cylindrical axis consistent so streaks stay horizontal. Coatings and the front element decide color and length.

Stop down and ovals become more polygonal. In a prompt, say horizontal anamorphic streak, name the hue, and demand oval bokeh, not round discs.

When to use it

A car cresting a wet overpass at night, headlights drawing cyan bars through a figure in a raincoat. Do not add horizontal streaks to a spherical 50mm close-up with round bokeh.

Compared with similar shots

Lens Flare covers ghosts, veiling, and spherical scatter. Anamorphic flare is the horizontal bar from cylindrical glass.

Anamorphic is the lens format itself: squeeze, oval bokeh, and the flare are consequences. Bokeh is the out-of-focus disc shape.

Oval discs support the claim. Round discs contradict it.

AnamorphicYou want the frame to announce it is a movie.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

HalationHighlights should bleed like film, not clip like video.

In film

Blade Runner lets neon and headlights write on anamorphic glass. J.

Abrams films push the horizontal streak until it becomes a signature. Super 8 (2011) uses the same family of bars as period scope language.

Prompt it

State squeeze and streak axis. Example: Horizontal anamorphic flares streaking through [Subject], cyan or magenta bars from headlights or neon, oval bokeh, 2x squeeze, not round spherical ghosts.

Use in Image Generator

Horizontal anamorphic flares streaking through [Subject], cyan or magenta bars, oval bokeh, scope cinema signature.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: generic lens flare or a spherical rainbow. Tell: round bokeh with a pasted horizontal bar that ignores source position.

Fix: match oval highlights, keep streaks horizontal, and lock them to a pictured point source.

Questions

What is anamorphic flare in film?

A horizontal streak from light hitting cylindrical anamorphic elements. It is optical, usually paired with oval bokeh from the same squeeze.

Anamorphic flare vs lens flare

Lens flare is any scatter in the optic. Anamorphic flare is specifically the long horizontal bar of squeezed glass, not circular ghosts or a general veil.

When should I use anamorphic flare?

When night points (headlights, neon, practicals) should write on scope glass. Do not use it on spherical lenses with round bokeh.

How do I prompt anamorphic flare for AI image or video?

Ask for horizontal streaks, a named hue, oval bokeh, and a point source in or near frame. Ban round discs and floating rainbows.

entries.title: Halation
entries.text:
Halation

Soft filtrationHighlight bloom

Halation in film is a reddish or warm glow around bright highlights caused by light passing through the emulsion, reflecting off the base, and scattering back into the image. It is a stock behavior, not a diffusion filter and not flare inside the lens.

Volume

Create this Halation

Narrative function

A lamp, a window, or a candle does not clip to a hard video edge. The highlight breathes.

A thin red or amber ring forms where the bright tone meets darker density. Fine contrast softens while faces and rooms stay readable.

Use it when the picture should feel developed on film: tungsten practicals, Super 8 lamps, a window in a small apartment. Tie the bloom to a point of view, not to every specular in the grade.

It is the wrong tool when you blur the whole frame equally and call it analog. If eyes go milky and there is no extra glow at highlight edges, you applied diffusion or defocus, not halation.

How it works

On film, skip or weaken the anti-halation layer, or use stocks and formats that show base scatter (some Super 8 and 16mm). In camera, keep highlights luminous but not clipped, and do not confuse this with a Promist on the lens.

Digital recreation should bloom only the brightest edges, often with a warm or red fringe, while preserving grain structure and eye texture. Prompt red-edge bloom around lamps, not a fog filter over the set.

When to use it

A woman beside a rain window, amber practicals breathing, the neon sign outside gaining a warm halo while her eyes stay sharp. Do not frost the entire frame and destroy highlight information.

Compared with similar shots

Lens Flare is scatter inside the glass, ghosts and veils that track a source into the optic. Halation is scatter in the film layers around a highlight already in the image.

Film Grain is the random silver or dye texture, not the glow. Vintage Cine Glass can add both bloom and falloff, but the physical cause of halation is the emulsion, not old coatings alone.

Film GrainThe image should feel developed, not rendered.

Vintage Cine GlassMemory, period, or beauty over resolution.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Master lets 65mm highlights bloom without turning faces to vapor. Barry Lyndon is grammar for candlelit tones that stay luminous instead of clipping.

Atonement uses soft summer windows around the country house. Those are highlight behaviors, not frames to copy.

Barry Lyndon 1975Soft pictorial light and luminous candlelit interiors.

Atonement 2007Soft, luminous summer imagery around the country house.

Prompt it

Bloom the highlight edge, not the whole room. Example: Halation glow around highlights on [Subject], red-edge bloom of film stock, lamps breathing, eyes and fabric texture preserved, not a global fog.

Use in Video Generator

A woman reads beside a bright summer window. Fine facial detail stays readable while window highlights bloom gently into the surrounding air. Subtle soft filtration, luminous skin without smoothing away texture, no fog overlay or global defocus.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: Promist, bloom filter, or shallow-focus mush. Tell: even blur, no red-edge, highlights crushed to white with no density.

Fix: confine the glow to bright edges, keep a warm fringe, and hold texture in faces.

Questions

What is halation in film?

A warm or reddish glow around highlights from light scattering in the film layers after bouncing off the base. It is emulsion physics, not a lens filter.

Halation vs lens flare

Flare is stray light inside the optic. Halation is a halo on the stock around a bright tone already photographed. One lives in glass, the other in the film.

When should I use halation?

When lamps and windows should bleed like film instead of clipping like video. Do not use it as a dream filter on every frame.

How do I prompt halation for AI image or video?

Ask for red-edge or warm bloom around specific highlights, preserved eyes, and film-stock behavior. Ban global defocus and fog overlays.

entries.title: Film Grain
entries.text:
Film Grain

Film grain in film grain cinematography is the random texture of silver halide crystals or color dye clouds in the emulsion, or a digital simulation of that structure. It is a developed surface, not a PNG overlay sitting on top of a clean render.

Volume

Create this Film Grain

Narrative function

The image is made of particles that change every frame. Shadows crawl.

Midtones have a living grain. Highlights are not a separate smooth plate.

Format and stock speed set the size: 16mm reads coarser in the frame than 35mm or 65mm. Use it when the picture should feel exposed and processed, not drawn.

A rooftop at blue hour, a winter platform, a handheld interior. Grain should scale with density, not stamp the same speckle on sky and coat alike.

It is the wrong tool as a default film look on a sharp digital plate. If the grain is identical on every frame, or floats above motion blur, it is a layer, not an emulsion.

How it works

On film, choose stock and format: faster stocks and smaller negatives show more grain. Push processing increases it.

Digitally, generate monochromatic grain that is denser in midtones and shadows, temporally unstable, and finer on larger implied formats. Do not sharpen after.

Prompt 16mm or 35mm texture, living grain, no overlay.

When to use it

A charcoal coat on wet slate at blue hour, 35mm grain in the dusk, chimney smoke breaking into particles. Do not paste coarse grain on an already sharp product still and call it developed.

Compared with similar shots

Halation is highlight bloom in the layers, not the particle field. Filmic Faded is a contrast and color decision (lifted blacks, reduced saturation), which can sit with grain but is not grain.

Light Leak fogs from the edge with unfiltered light. Grain is the stock's texture everywhere the image has density.

HalationHighlights should bleed like film, not clip like video.

Filmic FadedNot HDR. A print.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Revenant lets natural-light textures read as a developed image rather than a clean sensor. Roma is large-format stillness with a photochemical finish, not a grain storm.

Saving Private Ryan uses a harsher, tighter grain as combat stock language.

Prompt it

Specify format and that the grain is in the image, not on it. Example: Visible film grain over [Subject], 35mm or 16mm dye-cloud texture, temporally unstable, denser in shadows, not a cheap overlay.

Use in Image Generator

Visible film grain over [Subject], 35mm or 16mm texture, living silver, not a cheap overlay.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a repeating overlay, digital noise, or halation bloom. Tell: identical grain on every frame, speckle in clipped whites, or a wallpaper that ignores motion.

Fix: per-frame grain, format-sized particles, density-weighted, no overlay.

Questions

What is film grain in film?

Random texture from silver crystals or dye clouds in the emulsion. Size follows stock speed and negative area. It changes every frame.

Film grain vs halation

Grain is the particle structure of the image. Halation is a warm glow around bright highlights from light bouncing in the film layers.

When should I use film grain?

When the image should feel developed rather than rendered. Match grain size to format. Do not stamp one overlay on every shot.

How do I prompt film grain for AI image or video?

Name 16mm or 35mm, ask for living per-frame texture in shadows and midtones, and forbid a repeating overlay.

entries.title: Bokeh
entries.text:
Bokeh

round bokehoval bokehcat-eye bokehswirly bokehonion-ring bokeh

Bokeh in bokeh cinematography is the aesthetic character of out-of-focus rendering: the disc shape, edge, and smoothness of blurred points, not the mere fact of a thin depth of field. The glass, not a blur slider, decides whether those discs are round, oval, outlined, or swirling.

Create this Bokeh

Narrative function

A city, a string of practicals, or a wet street becomes a field of discs. Circular blades make circles.

Anamorphic squeeze makes ovals. Mechanical vignetting cats-eyes the discs at the frame edge.

Nervous, outlined, or onion-ring discs are also bokeh. They are just unkind bokeh.

Use it when the world behind or in front of a face should become light rather than information. One plane stays true.

The rest is the optic's handwriting. It is the wrong tool when you need the room.

If background signs, eyelines, or geography still have to read, creamy discs are hiding the scene. It is also the wrong word for a masked cutout with no optical discs at all.

How it works

Open the aperture, separate subject from background, and choose glass: spherical circles, anamorphic ovals, Petzval swirl, cat-eye at the edges. Point sources (practicals, speculars, rain catches) make the discs visible.

Distance and focal length set disc size. Prompt the disc shape and the source of the highlights, not blurry background alone.

When to use it

A close portrait in a cramped apartment, amber lamps and a magenta neon turning into circular or oval discs while the near eye stays sharp. Do not melt a wide master that still has blocking to read.

Compared with similar shots

Shallow Focus is the thin sharp plane. Bokeh is the look of whatever is off that plane.

Anamorphic turns those discs into ovals and often adds streaks. Rack Focus moves the sharp plane during the shot.

Bokeh can change as focus moves, but the pull is a different verb.

Shallow FocusNothing else is invited.

AnamorphicYou want the frame to announce it is a movie.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

In the Mood for Love turns crowded Hong Kong lamps into soft discs around faces. Her isolates Theodore against city lights whose character is the glass, not a painted smear.

Prompt it

Name disc shape and highlight sources. Example: Creamy bokeh field behind [Subject], circular or oval highlight discs from practicals, subject sharp, background as light not as a masked blur.

Use in Image Generator

Creamy bokeh field behind [Subject], circular or oval highlights, the world melted to light, subject isolated by glass.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a cutout mask or generic shallow focus with no disc structure. Tell: hair cut out like a sticker, no specular discs, background replaced rather than optically soft.

Fix: keep optical discs, cat-eye at edges if wide open, and a real distance between planes.

Questions

What is bokeh in film?

The character of out-of-focus rendering: circles, ovals, cat-eyes, swirl, onion rings. It describes how blur looks, not merely that something is soft.

Bokeh vs shallow focus

Shallow focus is a narrow depth of field. Bokeh is the optical handwriting of that blur. You can have shallow focus with ugly bokeh.

When should I use bokeh?

When only one plane may be true and the rest should become light. Do not use it when the background still has to carry information.

How do I prompt bokeh for AI image or video?

Specify circular or oval discs, name the highlight sources, keep the subject sharp, and forbid cutout edges or a smeared backdrop.

entries.title: Double Exposure
entries.text:
Double Exposure

CloningSplit matteSuperimposition

Double exposure in double exposure film combines two or more image records on one frame, in camera by winding back, optically in a printer, or digitally as an additive composite. Both pictures occupy the same emulsion or file unless a matte fully holds one off.

Create this Double Exposure

Narrative function

A face in a city. A ghost in rain.

Fireplace flames laid over a locked interior. Two times share density.

The result can be lyrical (memory, a second self) or purely practical (an element you could not shoot with the first pass). Use it when two records should coexist: a thought over a room, a spirit over a landscape, fire added later.

Superimposition is the family. Actor doubling with a split matte is one application, not the whole technique.

It is the wrong tool when you need two solid bodies that occlude each other, cast contact shadows, and pass objects. That is duplication or a split-matte composite, not a ghosted overlay.

It is also the wrong tool when a dissolve would carry you from one time to the next instead of stacking them.

How it works

In camera: expose, matte off part of the gate or shoot a full overlay, rewind, expose again with matched lighting. Optically: bi-pack or printer pass.

Digitally: additive mix or screened layers, or a hard split matte for twins. Lock the camera unless both passes share motion control.

Prompt two named images sharing one frame, optical overlay, not a hard cut and not a morph.

When to use it

A face superimposed over rain-soaked rooftops so memory and place occupy one still. Do not use a translucent overlay when two twins must sit at one table and pour tea.

Compared with similar shots

Dissolve is a temporal crossfade from shot A to shot B. Double exposure holds both at once.

Duplication makes two solid performances of the same body in one space, usually with mattes, not ghosts. Morph interpolates geometry from one form into another.

Overlay is not transformation. Match Cut joins two shots.

Double exposure never cuts.

DissolveMemory, passage, or a gentle death of a scene.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Persona stacks faces until identity is a density problem. The Tree of Life lays memory over photographed nature.

The Shining adds fireplace flames with a separate exposure. The Parent Trap and Adaptation use related splitting and doubling when two bodies must coexist, which is the cousin, not the same overlay.

The Parent Trap 1961The same performer appears as both twins in shared compositions.

Adaptation 2002Charlie and Donald occupy the same scenes.

The Shining 1980Fireplace flames were added with a separate exposure.

Prompt it

Name both records and the mix. Example: Double exposure of [Subject] overlaid with a second named image, faces in cities, a ghost in rain, optical composite in camera, both exposures visible, not a morph and not a split-screen join.

Use in Video Generator

A woman argues with an identical version of herself across a kitchen table. Generate each performance as a separate plate from the same locked camera and clean kitchen reference. Match eyelines and timing; keep their silhouettes separate. Composite them together with consistent shadows and no identity blending.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: dissolve, morph, or twin duplication. Tell: one image simply fades into the next, or two solid people with no shared density, or a face melting into a building.

Fix: keep both images present, set opacity or a matte on purpose, and decide whether the second pass is ghost or solid.

Questions

What is double exposure in film?

Two image records combined on one frame, in camera, in an optical printer, or digitally. Elements shot at different times appear together.

Double exposure vs dissolve

A dissolve is a transition that leaves shot A for shot B. A double exposure is a stack: both pictures remain visible in the same frame.

When should I use double exposure?

When two times, two selves, or two elements should occupy one image. Do not use it when you need two solid, occluding bodies.

How do I prompt double exposure for AI image or video?

Name both images, say optical overlay or in-camera double exposure, and specify whether the second pass is translucent or matted. Ban morph and hard split-screen unless that is the job.

entries.title: Rack Focus
entries.text:
Rack Focus

focus pullslow racksnap rackmultiple rackBascule de point

A rack focus moves the sharp plane from one subject or distance to another during a continuous shot, while the composition stays largely the same. Attention changes because the helical turns, not because the camera cuts or dollies.

Volume

Create this Rack Focus

Narrative function

A brass key is sharp on a desk. The woman in the doorway is soft.

Over about two seconds the key goes, her face arrives. Nobody moved.

The audience felt a handoff inside one space. Use it to change who owns the shot without cutting: pursuer and pursued, a clue and a face, a listener and the person who just entered.

A slow rack is a sentence. A snap rack is a jab.

It is the wrong tool when both planes must stay sharp (that is deep focus or a split diopter) or when the camera should physically travel. If details morph instead of going in and out of focus, the model invented a dissolve.

How it works

Mark two distances. Rehearse timing with the first AC.

Keep the head still for a clean demonstration, or coordinate the pull with a small move. Wide-open glass makes the rack readable.

Lens breathing may change field of view slightly. Decide if that is wanted.

Prompt: locked camera, named near and far subjects, a two-second pull, shallow depth of field, no zoom.

When to use it

Focus holds on a foreground key, then pulls to the figure in the doorway over about two seconds. Do not rack when the scene needs both faces sharp at once, or when a cut would be cleaner.

Compared with similar shots

Shallow Focus is a static thin plane. A rack is that plane moving.

Split Diopter keeps two distances sharp at once with a seam. Deep Focus keeps a continuous range sharp so no pull is required.

Push In travels the camera. The rack does not change the map, only the focus mark.

Shallow FocusNothing else is invited.

Split DiopterTwo distances must both be true at once.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Peking Opera Blues shifts focus from the pursued figure to the pursuing policeman inside one composition. The Graduate uses selective focus to organize Benjamin against the people around him.

The Player treats the pull as a long sentence of attention.

Peking Opera Blues 1986Focus shifts from the pursued figure to the pursuing policeman.

The Graduate 1967Selective focus organizes attention between Benjamin and surrounding figures.

Prompt it

Name both planes and the duration. Still: Rack focus between planes around [Subject], a two-second pull from foreground to the figure or the reverse.

Video: Focus racks from a named foreground element onto [Subject] over about two seconds, shallow depth of field, locked camera, no zoom.

Use in Video Generator

Locked composition: a brass key in sharp foreground on a desk, a woman blurred in the doorway behind it. Hold the key, then slowly rack focus to her expression as the key becomes soft. No camera move, no zoom, neither object changes position.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a cut, a morph, or both planes staying sharp. Tell: no defocus, details melting, or a zoom pretending to be a pull.

Fix: hold framing, send one plane soft while the other comes true, and keep identities stable.

Questions

What is rack focus in film?

A focus pull from one distance plane to another during the shot. The frame stays, attention moves. Also called a focus pull, slow rack, or snap rack.

Rack focus vs shallow focus

Shallow focus is the state of a thin sharp plane. Rack focus is the act of moving that plane from one subject to another.

When should I use rack focus?

When you need a reveal or a handoff of attention without cutting. Do not use it if both planes must remain sharp.

How do I prompt rack focus for AI image or video?

For video, lock the camera, name the near and far subjects, and give a duration (about two seconds). For stills, describe the pull as a pair of planes, one arriving, one leaving.

entries.title: Shallow Focus
entries.text:
Shallow Focus

Selective focusFaible profondeur de champ

Shallow focus keeps a narrow depth range sharp while foreground or background falls off. It is a depth-of-field choice made with distance, focal length, and aperture together, not a button labeled blur.

Volume

Create this Shallow Focus

Narrative function

The near eye is true. Ears, wallpaper, and the street outside go.

Isolation is optical: the world is still there, the glass has declined to report it. Intimacy is a byproduct of exclusion.

Use it when nothing else is invited: a ticket seller behind glass, a close-up in a crowded station, a face in an apartment. The blur should clarify who we are with.

It is the wrong tool for blocking that lives in depth, for geography, or for any beat where a background reaction still has to read. If hair is cut out like a mask and the backdrop is a smear without discs, you left photography.

How it works

8), longer glass or closer camera, and real subject-to-background distance. Keep the important eye as the mark, especially if the actor moves.

Bokeh character follows the lens. Do not treat aperture as the only control.

Prompt the stop, the sharp plane (near eye), and that the background is optically soft, not replaced.

When to use it

An elderly ticket seller, near eye sharp, station crowd reduced to unreadable shapes. Do not use it on a wide that still has to show who entered the far door.

Compared with similar shots

Bokeh is how the blur looks. Shallow focus is that the blur exists.

Deep Focus is the opposite: near and far both legible. Rack Focus starts from shallow focus and moves the mark.

85mm Portrait often produces this look because of distance and length, but any focal length can go shallow if you get close and open up.

BokehOnly one plane may be true.

Deep FocusLet the audience find the story in the whole room.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Central Station isolates portraits from busy surroundings. Her keeps Theodore in a thin plane against a soft city.

In the Mood for Love uses selective focus as crowding and privacy at once. The Master often holds faces in a narrow range against rooms that fall away.

Central Station 1998Portraits isolate individuals from busy surroundings.

Her 2013Intimate close-ups separate Theodore from his environment.

Prompt it

Name the mark and the stop. Example: Very shallow focus on [Subject], T1.4, near eye sharp, background dissolved into optical discs, intimacy by exclusion, not a cutout mask.

Use in Video Generator

An elderly ticket seller sits behind glass in a busy station. Tight portrait with the near eye sharp and the crowd reduced to soft, unrecognizable shapes. Tiny natural movements, stable eye focus, no plastic skin, no abrupt background replacement.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a subject cutout, or deep-focus staging with a fake blur. Tell: sticker edges on hair, both ears as sharp as the eye, no disc highlights.

Fix: a real distance gap, one eye as the plane, optical falloff, readable bokeh discs.

Questions

What is shallow focus in film?

A narrow distance range in focus, with foreground or background soft. It is depth of field, produced by stop, focal length, and camera-to-subject distance.

Shallow focus vs bokeh

Shallow focus is the thin sharp plane. Bokeh is the character of the out-of-focus parts. One is a depth choice. The other is glass handwriting.

When should I use shallow focus?

When only one person or object is invited. Do not use it when the room, a far doorway, or a background reaction still has to read.

How do I prompt shallow focus for AI image or video?

State T-stop, which plane is sharp (usually the near eye), subject-background separation, and optical blur rather than a masked backdrop.

entries.title: Deep Focus
entries.text:
Deep Focus

Extended depth of fieldGrande profondeur de champ

Deep focus in deep focus cinematography keeps multiple near and far planes legibly sharp in one image. It is a continuous depth of field, not merely action arranged in depth while the glass stays selective.

Volume

Create this Deep Focus

Narrative function

A hand stamps a form near the lens. A visitor waits in a distant doorway.

Both are readable. The audience may look at either without a pull or a cut dictating the choice.

Cause and effect share the room. Use it when the story is the whole space: a child outside a window while adults sign papers, a street and a face, two rooms through a doorway.

Staging does the directing. The lens declines to choose.

It is the wrong tool for intimacy that should exclude the world, or when light cannot support a small aperture. Two sharp planes with a blur belt between them are a split diopter or a composite, not deep focus.

How it works

Balance shorter focal length, smaller aperture, enough illumination, and subject distances that the stop can cover. Some famous deep-focus-looking shots also used in-camera composites.

The screen result does not prove a single-pass method. Prompt: everything sharp from a named near object to the far plane, no rack, no seam, continuous space.

When to use it

A clerk's hand in the near field and an anxious visitor in a far doorway, both sharp, locked wide. Do not claim deep focus if a blur boundary splits the frame in two.

Compared with similar shots

Shallow Focus isolates one plane. Deep focus refuses that isolation.

Split Diopter cheats two sharp distances with a visible or hidden seam and a soft belt. Layered Depth is compositional stacking.

It can be shot shallow or deep. Rack Focus would choose for the audience.

Deep focus leaves the choice open. Forced Perspective may need deep focus so the scale lie is not exposed by blur.

Layered DepthA shot should be walkable.

Split DiopterTwo distances must both be true at once.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Citizen Kane keeps young Kane readable outside the window behind the adults. Touch of Evil holds near and distant figures in the same legible compositions.

The Best Years of Our Lives uses deep space so a whole room can act at once.

Citizen Kane 1941The young Kane outside the window remains legible behind the adults.

Touch of Evil 1958Near and distant figures share strongly legible compositions.

Prompt it

Demand continuous sharpness, not two cut planes. Example: Deep focus on [Subject] and the far plane, near action and distant doorway both sharp, no rack focus, no split-diopter seam, the eye may wander.

Use in Video Generator

Locked wide shot of a courthouse office: a clerk’s hand stamps a form near the lens while an anxious visitor stands in a distant doorway. Both near and far action remain sharply readable, natural perspective, no rack focus, no artificial split-screen seam.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: split diopter or a composite of two sharp layers with mush in the middle. Tell: a vertical blur stripe, mismatched grain between planes, or a rack hiding in the still.

Fix: one continuous volume, matched perspective, both distances sharp without a join.

Questions

What is deep focus in film?

A large range of distances appearing acceptably sharp in one image, so near and far action can be read together without a focus pull.

Deep focus vs split diopter

Deep focus is continuous sharpness through space. A split diopter is a half-lens that sharpens two planes and leaves a blur seam between them.

When should I use deep focus?

When the audience should find the story in the whole room. Do not use it when isolation is the point, or when the stop would underexpose the set.

How do I prompt deep focus for AI image or video?

Name a near object and a far plane, require both sharp, forbid rack focus and a split seam, and keep perspective continuous.

entries.title: Forced Perspective
entries.text:
Forced Perspective

Apparent size manipulationPerspective trick

Forced perspective uses camera position, subject distance, and set geometry to alter apparent size or distance, and the lie exists only from the taking viewpoint. Bodies, furniture, and eyelines must agree or the scale collapses.

Volume

Create this Forced Perspective

Narrative function

A small adult sits at a table with a full-sized host. The table is built in two scales.

From one locked lens they share a meal. Move off the axis and the join shows.

The photograph looks ordinary. The measurements are not.

Use it to change size without a digital shrink: a hobbit beside a man, a grown actor in a giant childhood kitchen, a miniature city aligned with a live foreground. Fantasy stays inside a photograph.

It is the wrong tool for a free-moving camera unless the geometry is motion-controlled to match. It is also the wrong tool when you actually built a miniature of the whole world (that is diorama) or when you faked miniature scale with a tilted plane of focus (that is tilt-shift).

How it works

Choose the viewing position first. Place the small performer farther from camera, or the large one nearer, and scale the set pieces they touch.

Match eyelines and ground contact. Light both distances as one space.

Lock the camera, or move only on a path that preserves alignment. Prompt: in-camera scale by placement, shared table or floor, coherent eyelines, not a digital resize.

When to use it

A tiny adult guest and a normal host at one rustic table, locked camera, feet and hands sharing scaled furniture. Do not orbit the pair.

A new angle will break the alignment.

Compared with similar shots

Diorama photographs a physical model standing in for a large world. Forced perspective usually uses real people at different distances.

Tilt-Shift fakes toy scale with a thin focus plane on a real landscape. Deep Focus often supports forced perspective so both scales stay sharp.

Duplication copies a person. Forced perspective copies a size relationship.

Tilt-ShiftMake a city a model, or slice focus through a crowd.

Deep FocusLet the audience find the story in the whole room.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring seats humans and hobbits in shared compositions by distance and scaled props. Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind puts Joel child-sized inside enlarged rooms.

Those are viewpoint constructions, not frames to duplicate.

The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring 2001Human and hobbit scale relationships in shared compositions.

Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind 2004Joel appears child-sized inside enlarged childhood environments.

Prompt it

Describe the viewpoint lie, not a shrink filter. Example: Forced perspective with [Subject], scale altered by camera placement and scaled furniture, giant or miniature in camera, locked viewpoint, matching eyelines, not a digital resize.

Use in Video Generator

From one locked camera, a tiny adult guest sits beside a normal-sized host at a rustic table. Design the table and seating in separate scaled sections so their eyelines meet correctly. Stable hands, feet and contact shadows; no shrinking animation or distorted anatomy.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: tilt-shift miniature look, or a person digitally scaled with wrong contact shadows. Tell: feet hover, eyelines miss, blur betrays true distance, or the camera freely orbits.

Fix: one axis, scaled contact, matched light, deep enough focus to sell both sizes.

Questions

What is forced perspective in film?

A viewpoint trick: distance, staging, and set scale make people or objects look larger or smaller than they are. It holds from the taking camera, not from every angle.

Forced perspective vs tilt-shift

Forced perspective changes apparent size with geometry. Tilt-shift tilts the focus plane so a real scene looks like a toy. One lies about scale with placement. The other lies with focus.

When should I use forced perspective?

When two scales must share one photograph without a digital shrink. Do not use it if the camera must roam off the designed axis.

How do I prompt forced perspective for AI image or video?

Specify locked camera, two scales, shared furniture or ground, matching eyelines and contact shadows. Forbid free camera moves and simple resize.

entries.title: Light Leak
entries.text:
Light Leak

A light leak in light leak film is unfiltered light that reaches the emulsion or sensor without passing through the taking lens, usually through a gap in the body, magazine, or gate. It fogs from the edge or along a scratch in the film path, often orange or red on color negative because it hits the base side.

Create this Light Leak

Narrative function

The frame is wounded at the border. A wash of orange, red, or white eats density that the lens never saw.

It feels like damaged time: a Super 8 cartridge, a clock not seated, a magazine door. The pictured lamps are innocent.

Use it for memory, accident, or analog failure, when the camera body is part of the story. A leak can punctuate a cut or stain a whole take.

It is the wrong tool as a default nostalgia grade on a clean digital interior. If the wash sits in the middle of the frame and tracks a pictured sun, you are describing flare, not a leak.

If only highlight edges glow, that is halation.

How it works

Physically: open a gap at the magazine, leave a clock loose, or flash the film in loading. The fog often blooms from one edge and may shift as the film advances.

Recreating it: edge-based, warm, additive fog that can clip, unrelated to sources in the set. Prompt: analog leak from the frame edge, orange or red, emulsion wound, not a lens flare from a lamp.

When to use it

An apartment portrait with an orange bite coming in from the left, as if the cartridge failed, while the window practicals remain ordinary. Do not center a golden wash on the sun in frame and call it a leak.

Compared with similar shots

Lens Flare enters through the glass and ghosts the source. A leak bypasses the glass.

Halation is a halo around highlights already imaged. Film Grain is texture, not fog.

Light Flash is a temporal blowout of the whole frame, often as a cut. A leak is a spatial stain, usually from the edge.

HalationHighlights should bleed like film, not clip like video.

Film GrainThe image should feel developed, not rendered.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Spring Breakers uses analog damage, including leaks and blown edges, as party-memory texture. Super 8 (2011) treats cartridge wounds as period accident.

Home-movie Super 8 diaries are the grammar: edge fog, not a pictured lamp.

Prompt it

Put the wound on the edge, not on the sun. Example: Analog light leak washing [Subject], orange or red fog eating the frame edge, unfiltered light on the emulsion, not a source-linked lens flare.

Use in Image Generator

Analog light leak washing [Subject], orange or red flare eating the frame edge, a wound in the emulsion.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: lens flare or halation. Tell: the colored wash tracks a lamp in shot, or a red ring around a bulb with a clean frame edge.

Fix: originate the fog from a body gap at the border, independent of pictured sources.

Questions

What is a light leak in film?

Light that hits the film or sensor without going through the taking lens, usually from a gap in the camera body. It fogs the image, often from the edge.

Light leak vs lens flare

Flare is scatter inside the optic from a pictured or near-frame source. A leak bypasses the lens entirely. One ghosts a lamp. The other stains the emulsion.

When should I use a light leak?

When memory or analog accident should mark the frame. Do not use it as a default warmth filter, or when the sun in shot is the real cause.

How do I prompt a light leak for AI image or video?

Specify edge-origin orange or red fog, emulsion damage, and independence from lamps in the scene. Ban source-linked streaks.

entries.title: Vignette
entries.text:
Vignette

A vignette in vignette cinematography darkens, desaturates, or lowers contrast toward the frame edges because of optical falloff, mechanical vignetting in the barrel, a filter, or a later grade. Optical vignette follows the lens, while a post oval is a drawing.

Create this Vignette

Narrative function

The corners lose stop. Attention pools in the center without a spotlight on the actor.

Vintage wide glass and some anamorphics do this unasked. Cameo lighting can look similar, but that is a lighting plot, not falloff in the optic.

Use it to hold the eye in, to mimic old glass, or to admit that the field is darker off axis. Keep it gentle enough that the sides still exist.

It is the wrong tool as a heavy post oval crushed onto every wide. If the edges go to black like a spotlight and the falloff is a perfect geometric shape unrelated to the lens, you have a filter, not an optic.

How it works

Wide-open vintage glass, a wide angle on a small coverage circle, or an ND or grad at the edges. Cosine-fourth falloff is natural.

Mechanical vignetting is the barrel cutting the bundle. In a grade, darken corners with a soft, lens-shaped roll, not a hard oval.

Prompt: natural optical vignette, edges falling off, vintage falloff, not a post oval.

When to use it

A rooftop figure at blue hour, corners a stop down, center holding the coat and the city. Do not crush the sides of a group shot until the people at the edge disappear.

Compared with similar shots

Cameo Lighting lights a figure against a dark field. The darkness is in the set, not in the glass.

Vintage Cine Glass often includes natural vignette plus aberrations. Central Framing is a compositional choice that vignette can support.

Halation glows highlights. Vignette darkens edges.

Vintage Cine GlassMemory, period, or beauty over resolution.

Cameo LightingErase the world. Keep the person.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Barry Lyndon shows fast vintage glass with natural corner falloff in candlelit rooms. The Witch uses older optics whose edges go quietly, holding the eye in the clearing or the kitchen.

Prompt it

Ask for lens falloff, not a baked oval. Example: Natural optical vignette around [Subject], corners a stop down, attention pooled in the center, vintage falloff not a post oval.

Use in Image Generator

Natural optical vignette around [Subject], edges falling off, attention pooled in the center, vintage falloff not a post oval.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a circular crop, cameo spotlight, or a heavy social-media oval. Tell: perfect ellipse of black, subjects at the edge crushed, no relation to the lens.

Fix: soft, stop-based roll, keep edge information, match the glass.

Questions

What is a vignette in film?

Darkening or contrast loss at the frame edges from optics, the barrel, a filter, or a grade. Optical vignette is falloff. A post oval is an added shape.

Vignette vs cameo lighting

Cameo lighting is a dark set with a figure lit in the middle. A vignette is the frame itself losing light toward the corners, even if the set is even.

When should I use a vignette?

To hold the eye in or to match vintage glass. Do not crush the sides as a default filter, especially on groups and wides that need the edges.

How do I prompt a vignette for AI image or video?

Request natural optical falloff, a stop or so in the corners, and no hard post oval. Name vintage glass if that is the cause.

entries.title: Chromatic Aberration
entries.text:
Chromatic Aberration

lateral chromatic aberrationlongitudinal chromatic aberration

Chromatic aberration in chromatic aberration cinematography is color fringing from different wavelengths focusing at different distances or magnifications. Lateral CA puts red-cyan (or similar) fringes on high-contrast edges, worse toward the frame edge, while longitudinal CA puts different colors in front of and behind the focus plane.

Create this Chromatic Aberration

Narrative function

Cheap, wide, or vintage glass fails to put all colors on the same plane. A branch, a shoulder, a neon sign grows a red or cyan beard.

The optic is imperfect on purpose, or it is simply old. Use it when the glass should confess: lo-fi night, a dream that is optical rather than a grade, a wide at full aperture.

Tie fringes to contrast edges, stronger in the corners. It is the wrong tool as a full-frame RGB split, which is a channel offset, not aberration.

If the whole image is three layers of the same picture, you have a digital treatment, not CA.

How it works

Wide angle, wide open, simple or vintage designs. Lateral CA scales with distance from center.

Longitudinal CA shows as color bokeh (magenta in front, green behind, or the reverse). Recreate by fringing high-contrast edges, not by sliding entire channels.

Prompt: red-cyan fringing at high-contrast edges, stronger at the frame edge, cheap or vintage glass.

When to use it

A night overpass, raincoat against neon, red-cyan fringes on the brightest sign edges and the silhouette. Do not RGB-split the entire figure as if it were a channel offset.

Compared with similar shots

Lens Flare is scatter and ghosts, not edge fringes. Fisheye is extreme barrel distortion.

It can carry CA but is a geometry, not a color error. Vintage Cine Glass often includes CA plus haze and vignette.

Distortions are spatial warps. CA is a color-focus error on top of, or instead of, those warps.

FisheyeThe mind is warped, or the space is a dome.

Vintage Cine GlassMemory, period, or beauty over resolution.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Spring Breakers lets cheap-looking fringing and analog error sit on party lights. Music videos often push lateral CA as a wide-open night look.

Enter the Void uses optical error as subjective night, which is grammar, not a template.

Prompt it

Fringe the edges, do not split the body. Example: Chromatic aberration on [Subject], red-cyan fringing at high-contrast edges, stronger toward the corners, vintage or simple glass, not a full RGB channel offset.

Use in Image Generator

Chromatic aberration on [Subject], red-cyan fringing at high-contrast edges, cheap glass or dream distortion.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: RGB split, lens flare, or fisheye stretch. Tell: the whole subject is three colored copies, or only a rainbow streak with no edge fringe.

Fix: confine color to high-contrast edges, increase it off center, keep the core image registered.

Questions

What is chromatic aberration in film?

Color fringing from wavelengths that do not share a focus or a magnification. Lateral CA beards edges. Longitudinal CA colors the blur in front of and behind the mark.

Chromatic aberration vs lens flare

Flare is stray light making ghosts and veils. Chromatic aberration is a focusing error that puts different colors on contrast edges. One is scatter. The other is dispersion.

When should I use chromatic aberration?

When the optic should look imperfect: vintage glass, wide night work, a slightly untrustworthy image. Do not use a full-frame channel split.

How do I prompt chromatic aberration for AI image or video?

Ask for red-cyan (or named) fringing on high-contrast edges, stronger at the corners, from cheap or vintage glass. Ban whole-image RGB offsets.

entries.title: Infrared
entries.text:
Infrared

Infrared cinematography photographs near-infrared reflectance (roughly 700 to 900 nm), not heat, so foliage often goes pale, skies go dark, and skin can look waxy. It is a different slice of reflected light, still a photograph of the location.

Create this Infrared

Narrative function

The woods are white. The sky is near black.

Faces are wrong in a quiet way: veins, powder, fabric dyes all rewrite. The place is still Earth.

The spectrum is not the one the eye owns. Use it when a landscape should feel like another planet without leaving the location: a forbidden forest, a concert IR look, a surveillance still that is not green-tube night vision.

It is the wrong tool for hunting in total dark (that is image intensification) or for seeing body heat (that is thermal). If the image is green and noisy with blooming lamps, you have night vision.

If faces are ironbow masks, you have thermal.

How it works

Use an IR-pass filter and a sensor or stock sensitive to near-IR, or remove a camera's IR-cut filter. Light is still reflected sunlight or IR-rich tungsten, not emitted heat.

Expose for the Wood effect on leaves. Prompt: pale foliage, dark sky, waxy skin, near-infrared photograph, not green phosphor, not a thermal palette.

When to use it

A rider on a ridge, trees gone chalky, sky black, skin slightly unearthly, still clearly a daylight landscape. Do not render it as predator heat colors or as a green goggle feed.

Compared with similar shots

Night Vision intensifies residual photons onto a phosphor, usually green and grainy, as a hunting or surveillance eye. Thermal maps emitted long-wave radiation to a false-color palette.

Monochrome is visible-light black and white. Infrared can be printed mono, but its tonalities (white leaves, black sky) come from IR reflectance.

Night VisionSomeone is hunting in the dark.

MonochromeStrip to drawing.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Village used infrared film in the woods so the forest would read as another world while remaining a photographed place. Concert IR photography is the live-music cousin: pale skin, dark clothing dyes, no green tube.

Prompt it

Specify near-IR reflectance, not heat. Example: Infrared look on [Subject], foliage going pale, skies black, skin waxy, near-infrared photograph, not night-vision green, not a thermal palette.

Use in Image Generator

Infrared look on [Subject], foliage going pale, skies black, skin otherworldly, a spectrum humans do not own.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: night vision or thermal. Tell: green phosphor grain, or ironbow heat masks, or ordinary black and white with normal dark trees.

Fix: invert the foliage and sky relationship, keep it a reflected-light still, no goggle HUD.

Questions

What is infrared in film?

Photography with near-infrared light. Leaves often go pale, skies darken, skin and dyes shift. It is reflectance, not a heat camera.

Infrared vs night vision

Infrared film or IR photography is a spectral still of the world. Night vision is an image intensifier: residual light amplified onto a phosphor, typically green and grainy.

When should I use infrared?

When a real landscape should look spectrally alien: pale woods, black sky. Do not use it for goggle POV or heat detection.

How do I prompt infrared for AI image or video?

Ask for pale foliage, dark skies, waxy skin, near-infrared still. Explicitly forbid green phosphor and thermal color palettes.

entries.title: Night Vision
entries.text:
Night Vision

Night vision in night vision cinematography is image intensification: residual photons, and often a near-IR illuminator, amplified through a photocathode and microchannel plate onto a phosphor. The picture is typically green, grainy, blooming around lamps, with the framing of goggles, a weapon sight, or a camera in the dark.

Create this Night Vision

Narrative function

Someone is hunting or hiding. The world is a tube.

Speculars bloom. Resolution is poor.

Grain is the gain. You are not looking at a graded night exterior.

You are looking through a device that makes the dark usable. Use it as a point of view: a raid, a found camera, a basement with goggles on.

The green (or white phosphor) is the display, not a color grade on a normal sensor. It is the wrong tool for a moonlit scene, for pale IR woods, or for heat outlines.

If trees go white and skies black in clean daylight contrast, that is infrared photography. If bodies are warm masks against cold walls, that is thermal.

How it works

Motivate the device: goggles, rifle sight, security cam. High gain, scintillation, blooming highlights, limited dynamic range, maybe a circular or binocular mask, maybe an IR illuminator hot-spot.

Prompt: green phosphor, grainy intensification, surveillance or military eye, blooming lamps, not a teal grade, not thermal.

When to use it

A figure on a snow platform seen through goggles, green, noisy, lamps blooming, as a hunter's feed. Do not paint a normal night master green.

Compared with similar shots

Thermal sees emitted heat, not intensified light. Faces become temperature.

Infrared is a near-IR photograph of reflectance, often in daylight woods. Found Footage is the amateur or diegetic-camera wrapper that night vision often sits inside.

Night vision is the tube. Found footage is the alibi.

ThermalSee temperature, not light.

Found FootageThe operator is in danger too.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Hurt Locker uses intensification as a combat eye. Zero Dark Thirty uses goggle and raid imagery as the operation's seeing.

The Silence of the Lambs puts the audience in night-vision goggles in the dark.

Prompt it

Make it a device, not a grade. Example: Night-vision green phosphor of [Subject], grainy image intensification, blooming lamps, goggle or sight framing, surveillance or military eye, not a thermal palette.

Use in Image Generator

Night-vision green phosphor of [Subject], grainy, surveillance, found-footage military eye.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a green color grade, thermal ironbow, or infrared woods. Tell: normal contrast with a hue shift, or heat-colored people, or no grain and no bloom.

Fix: high gain noise, phosphor color, highlight bloom, diegetic device framing.

Questions

What is night vision in film?

Image intensification of residual light onto a phosphor, usually green and grainy, as goggles, a sight, or a camera in the dark. It is a device look, not a grade.

Night vision vs thermal

Night vision amplifies light. Thermal maps temperature. One blooms lamps and shows a grainy room. The other paints heat and can ignore visible lamps.

When should I use night vision?

When a character or camera is hunting in the dark through a tube. Do not use it as a green wash on a normally exposed night scene.

How do I prompt night vision for AI image or video?

Specify green (or white) phosphor, grain, blooming highlights, and goggle or sight framing. Forbid thermal palettes and ordinary night grades.

entries.title: Thermal
entries.text:
Thermal

Thermal imaging cinematography maps emitted long-wave infrared (heat), not reflected light. A microbolometer or similar sensor assigns a palette (white-hot, black-hot, ironbow) to temperature, so faces, engines, and blood read warm while cold metal and night air do not.

Create this Thermal

Narrative function

You are not lighting the scene. You are reading temperature.

A body is a mask. A recently used gun is a bright shape.

Walls may be dark. Visible lamps do not necessarily dominate.

The camera is forensic or predatory. Use it when the story is heat: a hunter's vision, search and rescue, a border raid, an alien targeting system.

The palette is a legend, not a grade. It is the wrong tool for green goggle work or for pale-leaf IR photography.

If lamps bloom and the room is grainy green, that is night vision. If foliage is white under a black sky, that is near-IR stills.

How it works

No key light in the usual sense. Contrast is delta-T.

Choose a palette and keep it consistent. Warm cores, cooler edges, possible bloom on the hottest spots.

Glass windows can block LWIR, so a face behind glass may fail. Prompt: thermal palette, heat as color, faces as warm masks, not green phosphor, not near-IR foliage.

When to use it

A rider and horse as warm shapes on a cold ridge, ironbow or white-hot, breath as a plume, stone dark. Do not render it as a green night-vision feed or as daylight IR woods.

Compared with similar shots

Night Vision intensifies residual light on a phosphor. Infrared photographs near-IR reflectance (white leaves, dark sky).

Thermal is emitted LWIR. Monochrome is visible-light grey.

A thermal image can look mono in white-hot, but its tones follow heat, not albedo.

Night VisionSomeone is hunting in the dark.

InfraredThe world should look like another planet that is still Earth.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Predator makes heat the alien's sight: bodies as warm figures in a cool jungle. Sicario uses thermal and related electro-optical views as raid and border seeing.

Those are device palettes, not looks to photocopy.

Prompt it

Map temperature, not lamps. Example: Thermal palette of [Subject], heat as color, faces as warm masks, ironbow or white-hot, search-and-rescue or predator vision, not night-vision green, not pale infrared foliage.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: night vision or near-IR photography. Tell: green grain with blooming streetlights, or white trees and black sky, or normal modeling from a key light.

Fix: temperature-based tones, warm bodies, cold surroundings, a named palette.

Questions

What is thermal in film?

An image of emitted heat mapped to a false-color or white-hot palette. It records temperature, not the light a normal camera would see.

Thermal vs night vision

Night vision amplifies light and usually looks green and grainy. Thermal paints heat. A cold dark room can still show a warm body on thermal.

When should I use thermal?

When the beat is temperature: hunting, rescue, targeting. Do not use it as a sci-fi grade on a normally lit scene.

How do I prompt thermal for AI image or video?

Name the palette (ironbow, white-hot), say heat as color, warm faces, cool environment. Forbid green phosphor and near-IR foliage looks.

entries.title: Slit-Scan
entries.text:
Slit-Scan

Star Gate effectTemporal slit photography

Slit-scan exposes moving artwork or a moving camera through a narrow slit over time, stretching space into streaks and corridors with time laid along one axis. The result is structured geometry, not a random particle tunnel.

Volume

Create this Slit-Scan

Narrative function

A slit is the only open part of the gate. Artwork or a light source moves relative to that slit.

Each frame or pass accumulates a thin slice. The stack becomes a corridor of color with a vanishing point.

Travel is not through a photographed street. It is through exposure.

Use it for passage that is not ordinary space: a stargate, a mind unspooling, a title that is time smeared into architecture. It is the wrong tool if you mean a kaleidoscope of mirrors, a time-lapse of a real street, or a nebula of sparks.

Random neon particles do not reproduce slit-scan geometry.

How it works

Classic optical method: slit mask, illuminated artwork on a track, camera or art in controlled relative motion, long accumulation. Digital: procedural streaks with a stable vanishing point, ordered planes, long-exposure character along one axis.

Prompt: slit-scan streaking, time smeared along one axis, a corridor of light, ordered perspective, no random sparks.

When to use it

A sustained passage through layered luminous planes that converge on a center, like the Star Gate. Do not fill the frame with unstructured particles and call it slit-scan.

Compared with similar shots

Time-Lapse samples a real scene at intervals. The world stays a world.

Slit-scan rebuilds space from a slit. Kaleidoscope repeats a fragment with mirrors.

That is spatial symmetry, not temporal smear. Motion Blur streaks moving objects inside a normal photograph.

Slit-scan is the photograph of the slit.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

KaleidoscopeOrnament, drugs, or chorus girls.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

2001: A Space Odyssey is the grammar: Douglas Trumbull's Star Gate, slit-scan corridors of light. Later films quote that structured tunnel.

They are not a license to generate fireworks.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968The Star Gate passage.

Prompt it

Ask for ordered temporal geometry. Example: Slit-scan streaking around [Subject], time smeared along one axis, structured corridor of light with a stable vanishing point, Star Gate language, no random neon particles.

Use in Video Generator

A sustained voyage through abstract planes of luminous geometry. Long parallel light streaks converge toward a stable central vanishing point, evolving through layered spatial corridors. Procedural slit-scan character, controlled acceleration, no literal starfield, random sparks or kaleidoscope cuts.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: kaleidoscope, starfield, or generic long-exposure sparks. Tell: chaotic particles, no slit axis, no vanishing point, or a mirrored flower.

Fix: one smear axis, repeating planes, controlled convergence.

Questions

What is slit-scan in film?

An optical process that exposes through a narrow slit while art or camera moves, accumulating streaks and corridors. Time becomes a spatial axis.

Slit-scan vs kaleidoscope

Kaleidoscope mirrors a fragment into radial symmetry. Slit-scan smears time through a slit into streaks. One is reflection. The other is temporal accumulation.

When should I use slit-scan?

When travel should not look like a photographed location. Do not use it as a stand-in for sparks, nebulas, or mirrored patterns.

How do I prompt slit-scan for AI image or video?

Request a structured light corridor, smear along one axis, a stable vanishing point, and no random particles or kaleidoscope cuts.

entries.title: Kaleidoscope
entries.text:
Kaleidoscope

Kaleidoscope cinematography fragments the image with mirrors or radial repetition so one subject becomes a symmetric pattern. The camera looks into angled glass, or the staging itself is a kaleidoscope: bodies arranged around an axis, often from above.

Create this Kaleidoscope

Narrative function

A shard repeats. A face, a limb, a lamp becomes an ornament.

Busby Berkeley built this with dancers and an overhead camera. A kaleidoscope adapter builds it with mirrors in front of the lens.

Chorus girls, jewels, a subjective break: the picture is multiplication, not smear. Use it when pattern is the point: a musical number, a jewel-box interior, a decorative fracture of a face.

It is the wrong tool for a stargate of streaks, for a simple birds-eye that does not repeat, or for a collage of torn edges. If there is no mirror logic and no radial repeat, it is just a busy frame.

How it works

Physical: kaleidoscope prism or three-mirror tube on the lens, or a mirrored set. Staging: radial choreography shot from Bird's-Eye View.

Keep a clear axis of symmetry and repeating shards. Prompt: kaleidoscopic fragmentation, mirrored shards, radial repeat of [Subject], not slit-scan streaks.

When to use it

A figure in a red dress multiplied into mirrored shards, jewel symmetry, like looking into a toy kaleidoscope. Do not stretch her along a vanishing-point tunnel and call it kaleidoscope.

Compared with similar shots

Slit-Scan smears time into a corridor. Kaleidoscope repeats space with mirrors.

Repetition and Pattern is compositional repeat in a normal photograph (windows, soldiers). Kaleidoscope is optical or staged radial multiplication.

Bird's-Eye View is the overhead angle Berkeley used. Without mirroring or radial design it is only a top view.

Repetition and PatternSystems, armies, hotels, factories.

Bird's-Eye ViewTurn life into a board game or a ritual.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Busby Berkeley numbers (42nd Street, Gold Diggers of 1933) turn chorus girls into kaleidoscopic geometry from above. 2001: A Space Odyssey also uses radial, jewel-like fragmentation in passages of the Star Gate, which is a cousin of the mirror, not the slit alone.

Prompt it

Demand mirrors or radial shards. Example: Kaleidoscopic fragmentation of [Subject], mirrored shards, radial symmetry, Busby Berkeley from inside a jewel, not a slit-scan tunnel.

Use in Image Generator

Kaleidoscopic fragmentation of [Subject], mirrored shards, Busby Berkeley from inside a jewel.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: slit-scan, birds-eye without repeat, or collage. Tell: streaks to a vanishing point, a plain overhead, or torn paper layers.

Fix: clear mirror axes, repeating fragments of the same subject, jewel symmetry.

Questions

What is kaleidoscope in film?

An image multiplied by mirrors or by radial staging so one subject becomes a symmetric pattern. It is repetition in space, not a time smear.

Kaleidoscope vs slit-scan

Slit-scan accumulates through a slit over time into streaks. Kaleidoscope reflects a fragment around an axis. Corridor versus jewel.

When should I use kaleidoscope?

For ornament, musical geometry, or a mirrored subjective beat. Do not use it when you need a structured light tunnel or a documentary overhead.

How do I prompt kaleidoscope for AI image or video?

Ask for mirrored shards, radial symmetry, and a repeating subject. Forbid slit-scan corridors and torn-collage edges unless those are separate.

entries.title: Light Flash
entries.text:
Light Flash

A light flash transition is a brief blowout of the frame to white or near-white, then a return, as if a bulb, explosion, or memory dump hit the emulsion. It is a temporal event, often a cut hidden in the peak, not a standing lens flare.

Volume

Create this Light Flash

Narrative function

The picture goes. For a few frames there is only density failure: a bulb, a muzzle, a Polaroid, a trauma.

Then the next image, or the same room, settles back. The flash is both a wound and a splice.

Use it when the cut should hurt: memory stings, explosions, still cameras in a crowd, a mind skipping. The white is the edit.

It is the wrong tool for a sun ghost that stays in shot, or for a smash cut that is only a hard join of two dark images. If the flare hangs and tracks a lamp, that is flare.

If you simply jump scenes with no blowout, that is a smash cut.

How it works

Overexpose a practical, a strobe, or a muzzle until clipping, or animate a white frame at the cut. Recovery can carry a lingering veil.

In camera, a still photographer's flash or a door onto daylight can do it live. Prompt: frame going to white then returning, bulb or explosion or memory sting, not a persistent source-linked flare.

When to use it

A hard flash blows out a face, then settles into the next memory, as in a sting cut. Do not leave a decorative streak parked on the lens after the white is gone.

Compared with similar shots

Smash Cut is an abrupt edit without a required white-out. A light flash is the white that can carry that cut.

Lens Flare is scatter that remains while a source is in the optic. Fade In / Fade Out goes slowly to black or white as a chapter mark.

A flash is fast. Iris closes a circle.

It does not blow the whole field.

Smash CutThe next image should hurt.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

Memento uses white flashes as memory dumps between Polaroids and the present. Saving Private Ryan lets muzzle flashes and overload wipe the frame as combat sting.

Raging Bull's camera flashes in the ring are the still-photographer version of the same blowout.

Prompt it

Make it an event with a recovery. Still: Blinding light flash over [Subject], a bulb, explosion, or memory cut, the frame going to white then returning.

Video: A hard light flash blows out [Subject] then settles back, as a memory or explosion sting.

Use in Video Generator

A hard light flash blows out [Subject] then settles back, as a memory or explosion sting.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: persistent lens flare or a smash cut with no exposure event. Tell: a rainbow streak that never whites the frame, or a hard cut in full detail.

Fix: clip to white (or near-white) for frames, then recover. Hide the splice in the peak if it is a transition.

Questions

What is a light flash in film?

A brief blowout of the image to white, then a return, used as a sting or as a cut. It is overexposure as an event, not a standing artifact.

Light flash vs lens flare

Flare is stray light in the optic that can last as long as the source is in play. A light flash is a temporal wipe of the frame, often covering an edit.

When should I use a light flash?

When a cut or a shock should be a wound of light: memory, explosion, still-camera flash. Do not use it as decoration on a quiet master.

How do I prompt a light flash for AI image or video?

For video, describe a blowout to white and a settle-back, and name the cause (bulb, muzzle, memory). For stills, show the peak or the recovery, not a parked streak.

entries.title: Projections
entries.text:
Projections

Reflective-screen projection

Projections in projection mapping film put a pictured image onto a surface that the taking camera then photographs: front projection onto a retroreflective screen, rear projection behind a window or windshield, or video mapped onto architecture. The projector is a light source, and the set is also a screen.

Create this Projections

Narrative function

Actors stand on a rocky foreground. Behind them a desert plate is thrown, coaxial with the lens, onto Scotchlite.

Or a car process shot: performers in a cockpit, a plate on a screen beyond the glass. Or a city that wears moving faces.

Media is the set. Use it when a large environment must coexist with live foreground, or when architecture itself is the display.

Front projection and rear projection are in-camera composites. Mapping is the same family with a three-dimensional screen.

It is the wrong tool when you mean a double exposure (two records in the emulsion, no projector) or a digital backdrop that never hits a surface. A generated image can imitate the look.

It cannot prove a projector was used.

How it works

Front projection: camera and projector aligned through a beam splitter, retroreflective screen, foreground lit so it does not wash the plate. Rear projection: a translucent screen behind the action, plate brightness matched to the foreground key.

Mapping: projectors registered to architecture, then recaptured. Prompt: projected imagery on walls or a screen behind [Subject], shared viewpoint, foreground lit to match, not a ghost overlay.

When to use it

A rocky foreground merging into a still desert panorama, performers lit to the horizon plate, locked wide. Do not drift the mountain independently of the camera, and do not stack a translucent face over the room unless you mean double exposure.

Compared with similar shots

Double Exposure combines two photographic records without a projector writing on a set. Practical Lighting is lamps in the scene.

A projector can be a practical, but projection is imagery, not just illumination. Rear-projection driving in Hitchcock is the same family as 2001's Dawn of Man front projection: a plate on a surface, recaptured.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Practical LightingLet the set light the face.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

2001: A Space Odyssey uses front projection for Dawn of Man landscapes. To Catch a Thief and Vertigo use process projection for driving conversations.

Blade Runner 2049 and Ghost in the Shell treat building-scale imagery as architecture.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968Dawn of Man environments combine foreground staging with projected landscape imagery.

To Catch a Thief 1955Driving conversations combine foreground performers with moving scenery.

Vertigo 1958Driving scenes use a controlled foreground against photographed surroundings.

Prompt it

Put the image on a surface. Example: Projected imagery crawling over [Subject] and architecture, a plate on a screen or faces on walls, foreground lit to match the projection, in-camera process not a double-exposure ghost.

Use in Video Generator

A small practical-looking rocky foreground merges into an immense still desert panorama. Locked wide camera, performers lit to match the horizon photograph, subtle boundary between physical foreground and distant projected landscape. No drifting mountain geometry or independently moving horizon.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: double exposure, or a floating hologram with no surface. Tell: a translucent overlay that ignores walls, mismatched vanishing points, or a background that parallax-slides against the foreground.

Fix: shared viewpoint, projection on a named surface, matched key, restrained plate motion.

Questions

What is projection mapping in film?

Throwing a pictured image onto a screen or onto architecture, then photographing the result. Front projection, rear projection, and mapped video all belong to this family.

Projections vs double exposure

Double exposure stacks two records in the image. Projection writes one record onto a physical surface in the set. One is an overlay. The other is a lamp that is a picture.

When should I use projections?

When the environment is a plate or the building is a display, and foreground performers must share that light. Do not use it as a synonym for any composite.

How do I prompt projections for AI image or video?

Name the surface (screen, wall, windshield), keep a common viewpoint, match foreground light to the plate, and forbid a ghost overlay or drifting horizon.
