entries.title: Morph
entries.text:
Morph

Morphing / Dissolve Effect

A morphing effect transforms one image, face, shape, or object into another by interpolating corresponding geometry over time. It is a continuous becoming, not a crossfade of opacities and not two exposures stacked.

Volume

Create this Morph

Narrative function

A face does not cut to another face. Vertices travel.

The nose, the jaw, the silhouette pass through illegal in-between states. Identity is unstable for a measured number of seconds, then a new form is solid.

Use it when the story is transformation: a liquid metal man, a mask that is anatomy, a person becoming another person. The audience should watch the change, not infer it across a dissolve.

It is the wrong tool when two images should merely trade dominance (dissolve), coexist (double exposure), or rhyme across a cut (match cut). If you still see both complete faces as ghosts, you dissolved.

If the cut is hard and only the outline matches, you graphic-matched.

How it works

Establish correspondence: eyes to eyes, contour to contour. Interpolate, often with a cross-dissolve of textures on top of the warp.

Duration is part of the grammar (a six-second become is a sentence). Prompt: [Subject] morphs into a named second form over N seconds, continuous transformation, not a dissolve, not a cut.

When to use it

A face becomes another face over about six seconds, features traveling, one identity at the end. Do not crossfade two full portraits and call it a morph.

Compared with similar shots

Dissolve changes opacity from shot A to shot B. Forms do not have to correspond.

Double Exposure holds both images. Match Cut joins two shots at a similar shape without interpolating the in-between.

Duplication places two solid versions of one person in a space. Morph turns one into the other.

DissolveMemory, passage, or a gentle death of a scene.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Terminator 2 interpolates the T-1000 through chrome and human geometry. The Mask treats anatomy as a morph target.

Willow (1988) and Michael Jackson's Black or White are early digital morph grammar: correspondence plus time.

Prompt it

Name both states and the duration. Still: Morph between [Subject] and another named state, face or body becoming, in-between geometry visible.

Video: [Subject] morphs into another form or face over 6 seconds, a continuous transformation, not a dissolve.

Use in Video Generator

[Subject] morphs into another form or face over 6 seconds, a continuous transformation.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: dissolve, double exposure, or match cut. Tell: two ghosts, a hard cut on similar shapes, or a texture fade with no warp.

Fix: require corresponding features to travel, show illegal in-betweens, land on one solid form.

Questions

What is a morph in film?

A continuous geometric transformation from one image or body into another. Features correspond and interpolate. It is not a fade and not a stack.

Morph vs dissolve

A dissolve is opacity. A morph is shape. In a dissolve you can see two complete pictures. In a morph you see one picture whose anatomy is traveling.

When should I use a morph?

When identity or matter is unstable and the change must be watched. Do not use it as a fancy dissolve between unrelated scenes.

How do I prompt a morph for AI image or video?

Name the start form, the end form, and the duration. Demand continuous transformation with traveling features. Ban dissolve and double exposure.

entries.title: Altered State
entries.text:
Altered State

Altered state cinematography makes the mind the location: smear, afterimage, wrong color, unstable time, optics and cutting that no sober observer would report. It is a bundle of techniques motivated by consciousness, not a single filter name.

Volume

Create this Altered State

Narrative function

Edges trail. Hue unhooks from the room.

A face leaves a stain. Focus and speed refuse to sit still.

The set may be an apartment. The picture is a nervous system.

Use it when perception is the plot: drugs, vertigo, dying, revelation. Pick a few physical tells and repeat them so the state has rules.

A smear plus a color unhook is a language. Everything at once is noise.

It is the wrong tool for a single clean optic (one fisheye, one flare) that the character would still recognize as the room. If the codec collapses, that is datamosh.

If two times overlay as density, that is double exposure. Altered state may borrow those, but it has to be motivated as seeing.

How it works

Combine a short list: long shutter smear, step-printed time, wrong white balance, afterimages, a diopter or a distorting optic, occasional overlay. Keep the body of the subject readable enough to stay in the scene.

Prompt: perception bent, edges trailing, color unhooked from the room, as if consciousness is slipping, not a random glitch pack.

When to use it

A close interior where the frame warps as a character slips, trailing edges, hue wrong, time sticky. Do not apply it to a wide establishing shot that still has to map the street.

Compared with similar shots

Dreamcore is a genre look of liminal rooms and childhood lighting gone wrong. Altered state is the perceptual event, often in an ordinary set.

Datamosh is codec collapse. Double Exposure is a stacked record.

Distortions are geometric lies in the glass. Altered state may include distortion, plus time and color that will not sit.

DreamcoreNostalgia with the safety removed.

DatamoshBreak the file on purpose.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

In film

Enter the Void binds camera, smear, and color to a consciousness that will not stay in a body. Requiem for a Dream uses speed, close optics, and cutting as intoxication and crash.

Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas is the wide-angle, wrong-color cousin.

Prompt it

List the perceptual tells. Still: Altered-state image of [Subject], smear, afterimage, wrong color, time that will not sit still.

Video: The frame around [Subject] warps as if consciousness is slipping, edges trailing, color unhooked from the room.

Use in Video Generator

The frame around [Subject] warps as if consciousness is slipping, edges trailing, color unhooked from the room.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: a single fisheye, a datamosh, or a dreamcore bedroom with no perceptual event. Tell: a clean room with one sticker effect, or total illegibility.

Fix: motivate two or three repeating tells, keep the subject locatable, let the room remain a room that is failing.

Questions

What is altered state in film?

Subjective photography in which smear, afterimage, color, and time report a mind rather than a sober room. It is a motivated bundle, not one optic.

Altered state vs distortions

Distortions are geometric warps from glass or air. Altered state may use those, plus color and time errors, as consciousness. Distortion can be sober (a peephole). Altered state is not.

When should I use altered state?

When the mind is the location. Do not use it as decoration on coverage that still has to be geographically clear.

How do I prompt altered state for AI image or video?

Name two or three tells (trail, afterimage, wrong hue, sticky time) and say consciousness is slipping. Forbid a generic glitch overlay and keep the subject readable.

entries.title: Anthropo
entries.text:
Anthropo

Anthropomorphic cinematography stages an object or animal as a performer: human scale in the frame, a gesture, an eyeline, reaction shots, as if the inanimate had a will. The camera does not need a face so much as an actor's grammar.

Volume

Create this Anthropo

Narrative function

A red balloon waits, follows, sulks. A robot tilts its head at a trash cube.

The object is not a prop in a still life. It is covered like a person: singles, looks, pauses.

Will is implied by blocking and eyeline, not by a drawn smile unless the story needs one. Use it to give a thing agency: a balloon, a machine, a relic, an animal shot as a colleague.

The rest of the scene should treat it as a presence. It is the wrong tool when you simply shoot an object from its own optical position (that is object POV) or when a tableau arranges bodies as a picture.

Anthropo is performance coverage of a nonhuman. Object POV is a camera mount.

How it works

Assign an eyeline height. Cover the object with the same sizes you would give an actor: wide for entrance, medium for dialogue, close for reaction.

Let humans look at it as a partner. Puppet, wire, or animation can supply gesture.

Prompt: an object or animal given human scale, gesture, or eyeline, the inanimate performing, not a POV from inside the object.

When to use it

A balloon at head height, held in a single, a child looking to it as if it might answer. Do not bolt the camera to the balloon and call that anthropo.

That is object POV.

Compared with similar shots

Object POV puts the camera in the object's position. Anthropo looks at the object as an actor.

Tableau freezes people into a composed picture. Anthropo keeps a will in motion.

Macro can isolate an object as texture without giving it an eyeline.

Object POVThe prop has eyes.

TableauHold the arrangement.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Red Balloon covers a balloon as a companion, with waits and follows that belong to a performer. WALL-E plays a machine with human gesture and eyeline without needing a human face.

Those are coverage choices, not mascots to copy.

Prompt it

Cover the thing like a person. Example: Anthropomorphic frame of [Subject], an object or animal given human scale, gesture, or eyeline, singles and looks as if it had a will, not a camera inside the object.

Use in Image Generator

Anthropomorphic frame of [Subject], an object or animal given human scale, gesture, or eyeline, the inanimate performing.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: object POV, a cute sticker face, or a still-life insert. Tell: the camera is mounted in the object, or the object sits as a prop with no eyeline.

Fix: assign a look, a height, and reaction coverage. Let others treat it as a partner.

Questions

What is anthropo in film?

Staging and covering an object or animal as if it were a performer: scale, gesture, eyeline, reactions. Agency is in the blocking, not necessarily in a painted face.

Anthropo vs object POV

Object POV is the camera from the thing's position. Anthropo is the camera looking at the thing as an actor. One is a mount. The other is a performance.

When should I use anthropo?

When a nonhuman should have a will in the scene. Do not use it for a mere product insert or for a true POV from inside the object.

How do I prompt anthropo for AI image or video?

Specify human scale, a clear eyeline, gesture, and coverage as if the object were a player. Forbid interior POV unless you want that cousin.

entries.title: Cinemagraph
entries.text:
Cinemagraph

A cinemagraph is a still photograph in which one isolated element continues to move on a loop (steam, rain on glass, hair, a blink) while the rest of the frame is frozen. It is not a freeze-frame of a whole shot, and it is not a full clip that happens to loop.

Volume

Create this Cinemagraph

Narrative function

The picture looks dead, then a kettle breathes. A coat is still.

Only the rain tracks the window. Time is allowed in one masked region.

The rest is a still. Use it when a photograph should refuse to fully stop: fashion, a poster that lives, a memory with one leak of motion.

The moving part must be plausible as a cycle. It is the wrong tool when the whole scene moves, or when all motion stops (freeze-frame).

If every element loops, that is an infinite loop of a shot, not a cinemagraph. If the loop is a boomerang of the entire take, that is a different toy.

How it works

Shoot a locked camera. Choose one motion that can cycle (steam, rain, flicker).

Mask that region in post, freeze the rest from a single frame, loop the live patch so the join is invisible. Prompt: almost a still, only one named element loops, locked camera, no other motion.

When to use it

A woman at a rain window, body frozen, only the rain and a thread of steam looping. Do not let her blink, the curtains blow, and the neon flicker all at once.

Compared with similar shots

Freeze Frame stops everything. Infinite Loop repeats the entire shot.

Boomerang plays a whole action forward and back. A cinemagraph freezes the majority and loops a patch.

Time-Lapse advances the whole world in steps.

Infinite LoopDuration without progress.

Freeze FrameEnd, joke, or evidence.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The form comes from fashion stills (Jamie Beck and Kevin Burg) and advertising, not from a single feature grammar. Fashion films and window displays are the well-known uses: one living detail in a still.

La Jetee is a cousin of stills and motion, not a cinemagraph loop.

Prompt it

Freeze the frame, license one cycle. Still: Cinemagraph of [Subject], almost a still, one isolated motion looping: steam, hair, a blink, rain in a window.

Video: Almost still on [Subject], only one named element loops, locked camera, seamless cycle.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: freeze-frame, full-shot loop, or a normal live take. Tell: several motions alive, a visible loop bump, or a frozen frame with no live patch.

Fix: one masked element, invisible join, everything else from a single still.

Questions

What is a cinemagraph in film?

A still image with one isolated looping motion. The rest is frozen. It sits between a photograph and a clip.

Cinemagraph vs freeze-frame

A freeze-frame stops all motion. A cinemagraph stops almost all motion and keeps one element alive on a loop.

When should I use a cinemagraph?

When a still should have one living detail: steam, rain, a flicker. Do not use it if the whole scene needs to play, or if nothing should move.

How do I prompt a cinemagraph for AI image or video?

entries.title: Collage
entries.text:
Collage

Collage cinematography builds a frame from torn, cut, or mixed pieces: different stocks, paper, print, and live action sharing one plane with visible joins. Edges are graphic, and the stack is a construction, not an optical blend.

Create this Collage

Narrative function

A head from one still, a building from another, newsprint, a painted sky. You can see the scissors.

Mixed grain, mixed contrast, maybe a bit of tape. One image was not enough, so the frame was assembled.

Use it when sources should remain sources: titles, satire, memory as scrapbook, a graphic sequence that refuses photographic unity. It is the wrong tool when two photographs should fuse as density (double exposure) or when live action and animation share a photographed space without torn edges.

Mixed media can do either. Collage insists on the cut.

How it works

Shoot or collect plates. Cut them.

Leave borders, torn fiber, misregistered printing, different grain structures. Composite with hard or torn masks, not a screen blend.

Prompt: torn layers, mixed stocks, cut paper and live action sharing one plane, visible joins, not a smooth double exposure.

When to use it

A portrait built from a live face, a city fragment, and newsprint, joins visible. Do not dissolve the same elements into a ghosted overlay and call it collage.

Compared with similar shots

Double Exposure is an optical or additive stack without scissors. Mixed Media is the broader family (animation plus live, print plus plate).

Collage is the cut-and-paste grammar inside that family. Split Screen divides the frame into simultaneous pictures with a designed border, usually live.

Collage can ignore a shared timebase.

Mixed MediaNo single medium owns the truth.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Terry Gilliam's Monty Python work is cut-out collage in motion. The Jinx titles treat documents and images as a stacked graphic plane.

Bruce Conner's A Movie is found-footage collage as a film, which is grammar for the cut, not a look to clone.

Prompt it

Show the joins. Example: Collage frame of [Subject], torn layers, mixed stocks, cut paper and live action sharing one plane, visible edges, not a smooth optical overlay.

Use in Image Generator

Collage frame of [Subject], torn layers, mixed stocks, cut paper and live action sharing one plane.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: double exposure or a clean split-screen. Tell: translucent blend, matching grain across pieces, or a hard live divider without paper or tear.

Fix: mismatched stocks, torn or cut borders, graphic stacking.

Questions

What is collage in film?

A frame assembled from cut or torn pieces of different images and materials, with joins meant to be seen. It is construction, not a seamless composite.

Collage vs double exposure

Double exposure blends records as density. Collage keeps edges: scissors, paper, mixed stocks. One is optical stack. The other is cut and paste.

When should I use collage?

When one photograph is not enough and the sources should stay visible. Do not use it for a ghosted memory overlay or a seamless twin shot.

How do I prompt collage for AI image or video?

Ask for torn layers, mixed film stocks or paper, live action plus cut pieces, and visible joins. Ban smooth double exposure.

entries.title: Datamosh
entries.text:
Datamosh

Datamosh is intentional codec failure: inter-frame prediction continues after keyframes are removed or broken, so motion vectors smear the previous picture into the next GOP and faces bleed into the following shot. The image is file wreckage, not a lens error.

Volume

Create this Datamosh

Narrative function

The I-frame never arrives. P-frames keep describing motion that no longer has a valid picture.

A mouth stretches into a wall. A cut happens in time but not in pixels.

Digital ruin is the style. Use it when the file should break on purpose: a music video, a corrupted memory, a broadcast that fails.

The smear should follow motion vectors, not a random RGB offset. It is the wrong tool for a stutter of whole frames (that is stop-stutter), for chromatic fringing, or for an altered-state smear from a long shutter.

If the image trails because the shutter was open, that is photography. If it trails because the codec predicted the wrong future, that is datamosh.

How it works

Encode with inter-frame compression, drop or repeat I-frames, let P-frames or B-frames run. The artifact is temporal and blocky, often with residual macroblocks.

Prompt: inter-frame collapse, faces smearing into the next GOP, codec wreckage, not RGB split, not film smear.

When to use it

A cut from a face to a city in which the face's pixels are dragged across the skyline by leftover motion vectors. Do not step-print the same clip or add red-cyan edge fringe and call it datamosh.

Compared with similar shots

Stutter / Stop-Stutter repeats or steps whole frames as a temporal rhythm. Datamosh destroys the picture between frames.

Altered State is perceptual and photographic. Chromatic Aberration is optical color fringing.

Datamosh is codec wreckage, not a general noise overlay.

Stutter / Stop-StutterThe mind skips.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

Chairlift's Evident Utensil is a well-known datamosh music video: GOP collapse as the picture. Other music videos adopted the same inter-frame smear.

Features rarely hold it long because it destroys coverage.

Prompt it

Break prediction, not the lens. Still: Datamosh of [Subject], inter-frame collapse, faces smearing into the next GOP, digital ruin as style.

Video: Datamosh corruption around [Subject], frames bleeding into the next, codec wreckage as image, not a shutter smear.

Use in Video Generator

Datamosh corruption around [Subject], frames bleeding into the next, codec wreckage as image.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: stutter, long-shutter smear, or RGB split. Tell: clean frame repeats, photochemical motion blur, or three colored copies of the subject.

Fix: blocky temporal bleed across a cut, leftover pixels from the previous picture, no new I-frame.

Questions

What is datamosh in film?

Deliberate video-codec collapse. Without a fresh keyframe, motion vectors smear the last valid picture into the next, producing inter-frame wreckage.

Datamosh vs stutter

Stutter repeats or steps complete frames. Datamosh lets predicted frames destroy the image. One is a rhythm of whole pictures. The other is a melt between them.

When should I use datamosh?

When the file should fail as the point: music video, corrupted feed, a digital breakdown. Do not use it as a substitute for optical smear or a simple jump cut.

How do I prompt datamosh for AI image or video?

Ask for inter-frame collapse, GOP smear, codec wreckage across a cut. Forbid shutter blur, RGB channel split, and freeze-frame stutter unless those are extra.

entries.title: Diorama
entries.text:
Diorama

Scale-model effectsModel photography

Diorama cinematography photographs a physical scale model so that it stands in for a much larger object or environment, with real light hitting real miniature surfaces. Scale is sold by texture, camera speed, depth of field, and movement, not by a toy-like tilt of focus.

Volume

Create this Diorama

Narrative function

A city, a ship, a hotel wing sits on a table or a stage, built at an inch to the foot or another ratio. The camera treats it as full size: enough stop for deep focus, a slow pass, fine windows, hard distant key.

Water, fire, and smoke are the hard parts, because fluids do not scale. Use it when a world should be tactile and built: a spacecraft, an industrial skyline, a storybook hotel.

The pleasure is that light is true on small surfaces. It is the wrong tool when you point a tilt-shift lens at a real city to make it look like a model, or when you align two live actors at different distances to lie about size.

Those are cousins. If depth of field is a thin band, the miniature will look like a miniature.

How it works

Build surface scale (panel lines, dirt, tiny lights). Light with a hard, distant key as if the sun were far.

Stop down. Move slowly.

For water and fire, high-speed capture can help scale. Prompt: miniature world photographed as full size, deep enough focus, tactile model surfaces, not tilt-shift toy blur.

When to use it

An orbital freighter as a detailed model, slow camera pass, tiny windows, deep focus against a black field. Do not add a thin horizontal band of focus that announces tabletop scale.

Compared with similar shots

Tilt-Shift tilts the plane of focus to make a real landscape look like a toy. Diorama is an actual model, usually shot deep to hide scale.

Forced Perspective uses live people and scaled set pieces from one viewpoint. Macro is close focus on small things as small things.

Diorama wants the small thing to read as large.

Tilt-ShiftMake a city a model, or slice focus through a crowd.

Forced PerspectiveChange size without VFX.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Blade Runner uses industrial miniatures for city and architecture. 2001: A Space Odyssey photographs spacecraft and stations as models.

The Grand Budapest Hotel uses storybook miniatures as a designed world. Those are model stages, not tilt-shift streets.

Blade Runner 1982The industrial cityscape and large architectural exteriors.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968Spacecraft and space-station imagery.

Prompt it

Photograph a model as a world. Example: Diorama view of [Subject], physical miniature, tactile surfaces, deep enough focus for full-size scale, slow camera, not tilt-shift toy blur.

Use in Video Generator

Photograph a practical-looking miniature orbital freighter as if it were enormous. Slow precise camera pass, deep enough focus for convincing scale, hard distant key light, tiny windows and layered surface detail. No shallow tabletop focus or fast toy-like acceleration.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: tilt-shift, or a digital city with shallow tabletop focus. Tell: a thin focus band, fast toy-like motion, coarse textures, fluids that look like pouring on a desk.

Fix: finer detail, deeper stop, slower move, scale-aware effects.

Questions

What is diorama in film?

Photography of scale models standing in for large objects or places. Real light on real miniature surfaces, sold as full size by focus, speed, and texture.

Diorama vs tilt-shift

Diorama is a real model, usually shot with enough depth of field to look large. Tilt-shift is a focus trick that makes a real full-size scene look small.

When should I use diorama?

When a world should be a built, tactile miniature. Do not use it if you only want a toy look on a real city, or a live-action size lie between two actors.

How do I prompt diorama for AI image or video?

Specify a physical miniature, fine surface scale, deep focus, slow camera. Forbid tilt-shift shallow bands and fast toy acceleration.

entries.title: Distortions
entries.text:
Distortions

Lens distortion cinematography warps space so straight lines bow, stretch, or melt: barrel, pincushion, mustache, extreme wide stretch, or a physical distorting optic such as a diopter, a bottle, or rain on glass. The lens is lying about geometry, not adding flare.

Volume

Create this Distortions

Narrative function

Walls lean. Faces balloon as they near the glass.

A hallway breathes. Space is not trustworthy.

The cause can be a very wide spherical, a fisheye, anamorphic mumps, heat shimmer, or a shot through a glass of water. Use it when the location should feel unsafe or subjective: a droogs' wide, a binge, a peephole, a fever.

Pick a distortion family and keep it consistent with the glass. It is the wrong tool for a clean normal-lens master, for flare without warp, or for a kaleidoscope of mirrors.

If color fringes without bent lines, that is chromatic aberration. If the whole mind is unhooked, consider altered state, of which distortion may be one part.

How it works

Choose the glass: 14 mm or fisheye for barrel, long glass for pincushion, anamorphic for mumps and wave, a close diopter for melt at the edge. Get too close to faces on a wide and perspective distortion adds to optical distortion.

Prompt: optical distortion around [Subject], stretched edges, melted geometry, named wide or fisheye, not a flare overlay.

When to use it

A close wide on a face in a tense interior, edges stretching, the room bowing, space untrustworthy. Do not keep a 50 mm rectilinear room and paste melted corners as a sticker.

Compared with similar shots

Fisheye is the extreme barrel member of this family, with a circular or strongly bowed field. Lens Flare is scatter, not geometry.

Chromatic Aberration fringes color on edges. 14mm Ultra-Wide distorts through field of view and proximity even when the designer corrects barrel.

Altered State may include distortion plus time and color.

FisheyeThe mind is warped, or the space is a dome.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

A Clockwork Orange uses extreme wides so rooms and faces are geometrically hostile. Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas melts space as intoxication.

Those are glass and proximity, not a warp filter parked on a normal lens.

Prompt it

Bend the space with glass. Example: Optical distortion around [Subject], stretched edges, barrel or melted geometry from ultra-wide or fisheye glass close to the face, the lens lying about space, not a flare pack.

Use in Image Generator

Optical distortion around [Subject], stretched edges, melted geometry, the lens lying about space.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: lens flare, fisheye circular crop without the scene, or altered-state color smear with straight walls. Tell: rainbow streaks, a round porthole sticker, or a clean rectilinear room with a melted overlay.

Fix: choose a lens family, bow lines, let near faces balloon, keep the warp attached to the optic.

Questions

What is lens distortion in film?

Geometric warping of space by the optic or by shooting through a distorting surface. Straight lines bow or stretch. The map of the room is no longer true.

Distortions vs fisheye

Fisheye is a specific extreme barrel lens. Distortions is the larger family: barrel, pincushion, anamorphic wave, heat, glass of water. Fisheye is one tool in that kit.

When should I use distortions?

When space should not be trustworthy. Do not use them on coverage that still has to be architecturally honest.

How do I prompt distortions for AI image or video?

Name the glass (ultra-wide, fisheye) or the surface, describe bowed lines and stretched edges, and forbid flare-only artifacts or a sticker warp.

entries.title: Duplication
entries.text:
Duplication

A duplicate subject effect puts the same performer in a frame more than once as solid bodies: twins, a self across a table, copies in one room. It is usually a split matte, motion control, or a locked-camera composite, not a translucent double exposure.

Volume

Create this Duplication

Narrative function

One person is not a single self. Two performances share a kitchen.

They argue, pass a look, fail to occupy the same chair. Contact shadows, eyelines, and any exchanged object are the hard problems.

Two similar-looking people are not automatically this effect. Use it when identity splits in space: twins, a writer and his brother, a man meeting himself.

The encounter should feel physically ordinary. It is the wrong tool when the second self is a ghost (double exposure), when the frame is simply divided (split-screen as the visible device), or when one body melts into another (morph).

If they cannot sit in depth and occlude, you have the wrong cousin.

How it works

Lock the camera or repeat the move with motion control. Record a clean plate.

Shoot each performance with matched light. Use a split matte where bodies stay apart, or tracked masks where they overlap.

Plan contact and handed objects as separate shots or as later help. Prompt: the same figure twice in one frame, solid bodies, matched lighting, not a ghost overlay, not a visible split line unless you want split-screen.

When to use it

Two versions of one woman across a kitchen table, distinct posture and clothing, shared shadows, locked camera. Do not stack them as translucent densities, and do not leave a vertical join down the table.

Compared with similar shots

Double Exposure is additive overlay. Ghosts, not two sitters.

Split Screen shows two pictures with a designed border, which can be how duplication is done if the join is visible. Seamless duplication hides the join.

Morph turns one form into another over time. Duplication keeps both.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Split ScreenTwo rooms, one moment.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Parent Trap seats one performer as both twins in shared compositions. Adaptation puts Charlie and Donald in the same scenes.

Enemy multiplies a man as encounter. The Social Network uses similar motion-control doubling for the Winklevoss pair.

Prompt it

Two solid performances, one space. Example: Duplication of [Subject], the same figure twice in one frame, twins of identity, solid bodies with matched light and contact shadows, not a double-exposure ghost, not a visible split-screen line.

Use in Image Generator

Duplication of [Subject], the same figure twice or more in one frame, twins of time or identity.

What usually goes wrong

Wrong cousin: double exposure, split-screen with a hard line, or two lookalikes who are not the same face. Tell: translucent stack, a seam down the set, mismatched grain or key, hovering hands.

Fix: locked or motion-controlled plates, identical identity, shared shadows, planned occlusion.

Questions

What is duplication in film?

The same performer appearing more than once in a shot as solid bodies, usually via split mattes or motion control. It is a spatial double, not a ghost overlay.

Duplication vs double exposure

Double exposure stacks densities so both images show through. Duplication composites two performances so each body can occlude, sit, and cast shadow.

When should I use duplication?

When one person must meet themselves as a physical other. Do not use it for a memory ghost or for a morph from one face into another.

How do I prompt duplication for AI image or video?

Ask for the same face twice, distinct poses, matched lighting, contact shadows, locked camera. Forbid translucent overlay and a visible split line unless split-screen is the point.

entries.title: Echo Print
entries.text:
Echo Print

An echo print is an echo print effect that leaves a ghosted afterimage offset in time or register, so the last pose is still printed on this frame. The ghost is a stain of a previous exposure, not a second complete picture sharing the same plane.

Volume

Create this Echo Print

Narrative function

Use it when a gesture has already happened and the present cannot shake it. A head turns and the old profile hangs a few pixels away.

A step leaves a faint body where the foot was. Time reads as a registration error.

It is the wrong tool for a clean double of two living people in conversation. If both images are fully exposed and equally sharp, you shot a superimposition, not a stain.

How it works

Keep the camera locked or on a short path. Copy the previous frame, offset it along the motion vector by a few pixels or a few milliseconds, and print it at lower opacity.

Optical printers did this with a slight mis-register. Video echo does it with delay.

One key still lights the live body. The ghost has no second key.

Prompt an afterimage offset in time or register, and say that the last frame is still printed on this one.

When to use it

Use it for the beat after a look, a blow, or a departure, when the last pose should remain as a stain. Do not use it to introduce a twin who must occupy the room as a solid person.

Compared with similar shots

Double Exposure combines two complete pictures. An echo print is a faded offset of the same action.

Step Printing repeats discrete frames to slow or stutter a take. The echo is a smear of register, not a held frame.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Step PrintingLonging that cannot move at normal speed.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Experimental optical printing and title-design ghosts are the grammar: a credit or a figure that leaves a trail of itself. Video-echo music videos do the same with delay.

These are uses of the stain, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Write the still as a photochemical hold, then name the ghost. Quote: Echo print of [Subject], a ghosted afterimage offset in time or register, the last frame still printed on this one.

For video: Afterimages of [Subject] trail the present, an echo print of the previous moment. Name the offset direction.

Ban a second full scene.

Use in Video Generator

Afterimages of [Subject] trail the present, an echo print of the previous moment.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Double Exposure. The tell is two equally solid bodies, both keyed, both sharp.

The fix is one live subject and a fainter, offset copy of the same pose, no second lamp.

Questions

What is echo print in film?

Echo print leaves a ghosted afterimage offset in time or register, as if the last frame were still printed on this one. The past of the gesture remains visible as a stain.

Echo print vs double exposure

Double exposure combines two complete images. Echo print reprints a delayed or mis-registered copy of the same action at lower strength. One is two pictures. The other is a trail.

When should I use echo print?

Use it when a movement should leave a mark: a turn, a blow, a person already gone. Skip it when you need two solid people sharing a scene.

How do I prompt echo print for AI image or video?

Name the subject, then demand a ghosted afterimage offset in time or register. Keep one key. Say the last frame is still printed on this one. For video, afterimages should trail the present pose.

entries.title: Feedback
entries.text:
Feedback

Video feedback is made by pointing a camera at its own live output so the picture nests into a recursive corridor of the same face. Each generation is a rephotograph of the monitor, with bloom, lag, and a tunnel of shrinking frames.

Volume

Create this Feedback

Narrative function

The medium stares at itself. A face on a tube is recaptured, recaptured again, and the room becomes a hallway of the same look.

Use it when the story is about watching, broadcast, or a mind that cannot get out of the signal. It is the wrong tool for a simple loop of action.

If the last frame merely sews to the first, you have a cycle in time, not a camera eating its monitor.

How it works

Aim the taking lens at a playback screen that shows the live feed. A slight off-axis angle builds a corridor.

Dead-on nesting builds rectangles inside rectangles. Gain, lag, and the phosphor or pixel bloom set how fast the tunnel eats itself.

The subject is usually close to the screen so the first generation is readable. Prompt video feedback around the subject: camera looking into its own output, infinite corridor of the same face.

When to use it

Use it when a person is trapped in a transmission, a title, or a night of monitors. Do not use it as wallpaper behind a dialogue scene that still needs geography.

Compared with similar shots

Kaleidoscope mirrors facets of one image into symmetry. Feedback nests generations of the same capture.

Infinite Loop sews the last frame to the first in time. Feedback is optical recursion, not a cycle of action.

KaleidoscopeOrnament, drugs, or chorus girls.

Infinite LoopDuration without progress.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

1960s tape experiments pointed cameras at monitors until the image tunnelled. The Doctor Who howlaround titles are the famous broadcast version.

Music videos still use the same recursive corridor. Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Video feedback around [Subject], camera looking into its own output, infinite corridor of the same face. For video: Recursive video feedback of [Subject], the image eating itself into a tunnel.

Name the first generation (a face, a room) so the nest has a source.

Use in Video Generator

Recursive video feedback of [Subject], the image eating itself into a tunnel.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Kaleidoscope or a simple video loop. The tell is mirrored wedges or a repeating walk with no nested screen.

The fix is a camera aimed at its own output, generations shrinking down a tunnel.

Questions

What is feedback in film?

Video feedback is a camera looking into its own output so the image rephotographs itself into a nested corridor. Bloom, lag, and a tunnel of the same face are the picture.

Feedback vs kaleidoscope

A kaleidoscope mirrors one image into symmetric facets. Feedback recaptures the live picture from a monitor, stacking generations rather than folding the frame.

When should I use feedback?

Use it when the story is the signal watching itself: broadcast, hypnosis, a face trapped in a tube. Skip it for ordinary looping action.

How do I prompt feedback for AI image or video?

Say video feedback, camera looking into its own output, infinite corridor of the same face. For motion, the image should eat itself into a tunnel. Keep a readable first generation.

entries.title: Floating UI
entries.text:
Floating UI

Floating UI, or HUD overlay cinematography, places readable interface, callouts, and data planes in the air of the scene so information lives in space, not only on a physical screen. The cockpit is the room.

Volume

Create this Floating UI

Narrative function

A hand reaches into a diagram. Callouts hang beside a face.

The camera can dolly and the panels should parallax against the walls. Use it when the character is working with data as if it were furniture.

It is the wrong tool when type is glued to the frame like a broadcast bug. If the graphics do not occupy 3D space, you made a lower-third, not a HUD in the air.

How it works

Photograph the subject with a real key in the room. Composite interface planes with their own vanishing points, a few centimeters to a few meters in front of the face.

If the camera moves, the panels must parallax. Type stays sharp enough to read.

A faint self-illumination on the planes is allowed. It should not replace the key on the skin.

Prompt floating UI over the subject: HUD, callouts, and interface planes in 3D space, the screen as a cockpit.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a pilot, surgeon, or detective is reading the air. Do not use it as decorative chrome on a portrait that has no data to parse.

Compared with similar shots

Projections throw pictures onto walls and bodies. Floating UI hangs panels in space.

Video Game borrows playable camera grammar and HUD as game UI. Floating UI can live in live-action space without becoming a navigable engine.

Video GameThe world is playable.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

Minority Report treats data as planes a body can shove. Iron Man puts callouts in the helmet's air.

Both are grammar for readable interface in 3D, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Floating UI over [Subject], HUD, callouts, and interface planes in 3D space, the screen as a cockpit. Name what the panels say in plain language, keep type sharp, and say the planes parallax if the camera moves.

Ban unreadable scribble.

Use in Image Generator

entries.title: Focal Shift
entries.text:
Focal Shift

focus pullslow racksnap rackmultiple rack

A focal shift moves the plane of sharpness from one subject or distance to another during the shot, so attention travels as a pull. The camera body can stay put, and only the focus mechanism walks the depth.

Volume

Create this Focal Shift

Narrative function

Someone in the foreground owns the frame, then the helix turns and a face in the room takes over. No cut.

The blur itself is the sentence. Use it when who matters changes while geography stays.

It is the wrong tool if both planes must stay readable at once, or if you only need a static shallow portrait. If nothing is sharp at either end, you did not shift focus.

You lost it.

How it works

Mark two distances. Keep depth of field shallow enough that only one plane is crisp, often a 50mm to 85mm near T2.

A follow-focus or remote motor walks the helical from A to B. The camera is usually locked or slow so the pull is the only event.

Lens breathing may thicken the image slightly as glass moves. Prompt a focal shift: the plane of sharpness traveling from one fact to another.

For video, pull from a foreground object onto the subject, or the reverse.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a glass, a gun, or a listener in the foreground yields to the person who must answer. Do not use it as decoration on a single face with no second plane.

Compared with similar shots

Rack Focus is the standard two-mark transfer, often about two seconds, composition held. Focal shift is the traveling plane as the event, including a slow rack, a snap rack, or several racks in a row.

Shallow Focus is a state: one plane already sharp. A shift is the move between states.

Rack FocusChange who owns the shot without cutting.

Shallow FocusNothing else is invited.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Graduate organizes attention between Benjamin and the figures around him by selective focus. There Will Be Blood uses the same grammar in hard interiors: who is true in the room changes without a cut.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Focal shift on [Subject], the plane of sharpness traveling from one fact to another, attention as a pull. Video: Focus pulls from a foreground object onto [Subject], or the reverse.

Name both planes, the lens, and that the camera body stays put.

Use in Video Generator

Focus pulls from a foreground object onto [Subject], or the reverse.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a cut, or a morph of detail during the pull. The tell is both planes sharp, or the face warping as focus moves.

The fix is two marked distances, shallow field, and a clean travel of the plane.

Questions

What is focal shift in film?

A focal shift moves the plane of sharpness from one subject or distance to another during a shot. Attention changes without cutting, as a pull through depth.

Focal shift vs rack focus

Rack focus is the textbook two-mark pull with the composition held. Focal shift is the same physics treated as the event itself, including slow, snap, or multiple racks. One is the procedure. The other is the traveling plane.

When should I use focal shift?

Use it when a foreground fact must hand the shot to a face, or the reverse, inside one take. Skip it if you need both planes sharp, or if there is no second subject.

How do I prompt focal shift for AI image or video?

Name both planes. Say the plane of sharpness travels from one fact to another while the camera body stays. For video, pull from a foreground object onto the subject, or the reverse.

entries.title: Generative
entries.text:
Generative

Generative visuals show process: forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration, so cinema is made by a system rather than only by a finished photograph. Making is visible.

Volume

Create this Generative

Narrative function

A body, a city, or a cloud is not posed. It is grown.

Cells, grains, or agents iterate until a figure appears. Use it when the point is how the image becomes, not only what it depicts.

It is the wrong tool for a codec wound or a person turning into a beast. If the look is smashed motion vectors, you want datamosh.

If a body becomes another body in continuous view, you want a transformation.

How it works

Treat the forming matter as something you can light. Name the rule (particles, iteration, grown geometry), the scale of the bits, and a hard or soft source that rakes them.

The camera can be locked so the growth is the move. Keep a readable subject so the system has an object.

Prompt a generative image of the subject: forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration, cinema made by a system.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a world or a face is still assembling. Do not use it as a style wash on a finished portrait that never needed a rule.

Compared with similar shots

Datamosh is deliberate compression failure: I-frames gone, motion vectors smeared. Generative growth is a rule, not a wound in the file.

Transformation changes a body or room in continuous view. Generative imagery shows the system that builds the picture.

DatamoshBreak the file on purpose.

TransformationThe change is the scene.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Koyaanisqatsi-adjacent process films let systems and time grow the image. Music-video generative sequences make iteration the event on screen.

Grammar for process, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Generative image of [Subject], forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration, cinema made by a system. Name the rule and the light on the bits.

Keep the subject recognizable at the end of the growth.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are Datamosh and a generic melt. The tell is blocky codec smear, or a face liquefying with no rule.

The fix is named iteration, countable bits, and a subject the system is growing toward.

Questions

What is generative in film?

Generative visuals show process rather than only a finished result. Forms are grown by rule, particles, and iteration, so the system that makes the picture is visible.

Generative vs datamosh

Datamosh breaks the file on purpose. Generative work builds an image by iteration. One is a codec artifact. The other is a rule you can light.

When should I use generative?

Use it when becoming-by-rule is the scene: a city assembling, a body grown from particles. Skip it as a filter on a still that is already complete.

How do I prompt generative for AI image or video?

entries.title: Levitation
entries.text:
Levitation

Wire workWire removal

A levitation shot holds a body or object in a quiet impossible hover, refusing ordinary gravity while support is hidden or removed. Hair and cloth still hang, and the gap under the feet is the proof.

Volume

Create this Levitation

Narrative function

Someone leaves the floor and stays. The room does not drop away.

The camera often holds so we can read the air under the shoes. Use it when weight is optional and the performance should still look human: a takeoff, an apex, a landing.

It is the wrong tool for a fall. If the body is going down, even slowly, you want a floating fall.

If the camera itself is dropping, you want falling.

How it works

Support the performer on wires, a crane, or a hidden platform, then remove the rig in a clean plate. Keep a hard side-key so the gap under the feet is visible.

Cloth and hair hang downward because gravity still acts on fabric. Specify launch, trajectory, apex, and landing rather than a vague request to fly.

Prompt levitation of the subject: body or object refusing gravity, a quiet impossible hover, no visible support.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a person hangs in a room, on a rooftop, or over a street and the hover is the fact. Do not use it for a drop that must still feel like disaster.

Compared with similar shots

Falling drops the camera or the body with real weight, ground rising. Bullet Time orbits a pose that is frozen in time.

Levitation is a sustained hover with a living performance. Floating Fall still goes down.

This does not.

FallingGravity is the plot.

Bullet TimeA moment is so important it becomes architecture.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon keeps human effort inside rooftop and bamboo flight. The Matrix suspends combat so a body can hang and strike.

Mary Poppins arrives by an impossible hold in the air. Grammar for hover, not frames to copy.

Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon 2000Rooftop movement and the bamboo-forest duel.

The Matrix 1999Suspended and extended movements during combat.

Prompt it

Levitation of [Subject], body or object refusing gravity, a quiet impossible hover. Video: [Subject] hangs in air, slow drift, no visible support.

Name the gap under the feet, the hang of cloth, and takeoff or landing if they exist.

Use in Video Generator

A fictional acrobat crosses between two low rooftops in one graceful extended leap. Clear push-off, smooth rising arc, brief suspension and weighted landing with knees absorbing impact. Loose fabric follows the body with delay. Fixed wide camera, consistent architecture, no teleportation or rubber limbs.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a balloon hover or a fall shot in slow motion. The tell is missing takeoff and landing, rubber limbs, or cloth that floats as if underwater.

The fix is a readable gap, downward hang of fabric, and a human push-off or settle.

Questions

What is levitation in film?

A levitation shot holds a body or object in a hover that ordinary jumping cannot sustain. Support is hidden or removed. Hair and cloth still hang.

Levitation vs floating fall

Levitation stays up. A floating fall still descends, with delayed gravity on hair and coat. One is a hover. The other is a drop with the clock wrong.

When should I use levitation?

Use it when a person or object must hang in air as a quiet fact, with a human takeoff or landing. Skip it when the story is the ground coming up.

entries.title: Masking
entries.text:
Masking

Masking cinematography uses a matte, a viewfinder object, or a graphic window so looking is visible as a shape cutting the picture. We see through binoculars, a keyhole, or a hard-edged hole.

Volume

Create this Masking

Narrative function

The audience is made to look as a character looks. A circle of night, a door slot, a camera's own frame-lines.

The surround is black or graphic. The photograph lives only in the hole.

It is the wrong tool when you merely want a tighter shot, or when the container itself should widen. If the outer bounds of the movie change ratio, that is a ratio switch.

If a doorway is simply in the set, that is a frame within a frame.

How it works

Put a physical mask in front of the lens (binoculars, a cutout, an iris board) or add a hard matte in optical printing. The interior of the hole is the exposure.

The surround stays opaque. Keep the subject composed for that shape, not for the full sensor.

Light the interior as a real scene. The mask does not need its own key.

Prompt a masked frame around the subject: a shape cutting the picture, binoculars, a keyhole, a graphic window.

When to use it

Use it for the beat of spying, peeping, or a title that looks through an object. Do not use it as a fancy crop on a scene that is not about looking.

Compared with similar shots

Frame within Frame uses architecture already in the room: a window, a door, a mirror. Masking cuts the picture with a shape that is the act of looking.

Iris opens or closes a circle as a transition. A masked binocular hole can sit for the whole shot.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

IrisPoint with the mask itself.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Kill Bill looks through coffin slots and tight graphic holes. The Grand Budapest Hotel boxes looking as a designed window.

Grammar for seeing-as-object, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Masked frame around [Subject], a shape cutting the picture, binoculars, a keyhole, a graphic window. Name the shape, keep the interior photographed, and keep the surround opaque.

Do not stretch the image to fill the hole.

Use in Image Generator

Masked frame around [Subject], a shape cutting the picture, binoculars, a keyhole, a graphic window.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are a Wide Shot with a vignette, or a Ratio Switch. The tell is a soft dark edge, or the whole frame widening.

The fix is a hard shape, a hole, and a scene composed for that hole.

Questions

What is masking in film?

Masking cuts the picture with a shape so looking is visible as an object: binoculars, a keyhole, a graphic window. The photograph lives inside the hole.

Masking vs iris

An iris is usually a circular transition that opens or closes. Masking is a persistent shape through which we look. One is a join. The other is a viewfinder.

When should I use masking?

Use it when the act of looking should be an object in the shot. Skip it when you only need a closer framing or a change of aspect ratio.

How do I prompt masking for AI image or video?

entries.title: Mixed Media
entries.text:
Mixed Media

Mixed media film combines live action with type, illustration, and stock in one plane so no single capture method owns the truth of the frame. Media collide rather than dissolve into one photograph.

Volume

Create this Mixed Media

Narrative function

A face is a photograph. The wall is a drawing.

A headline sits on the glass. Use it when the story is already a pile of documents, broadcasts, and drawings, and the cut would lie by smoothing them.

It is the wrong tool for a single elegant composite that should feel like one camera. If every layer is the same still torn into pieces, you are closer to collage.

If the only extra layer is words as objects, you are closer to typography.

How it works

Shoot or generate a live-action plate with a real key. Add illustration, type, and stock as separate layers with visible edges: torn, keyed, or butted.

Lighting does not have to match across media. The mismatch is evidence of different sources.

Keep one subject readable so the collision has a center. Prompt mixed media around the subject: live action, type, illustration, and stock colliding in one plane.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when news, memory, and the body cannot agree on one medium. Do not use it as a sticker pack on a scene that still wants photochemical unity.

Compared with similar shots

Collage layers stills and textures into one picture. Mixed media insists on different capture modes in the same plane.

Typography puts words in the world as objects. Mixed media can include type, but type is only one of the colliding sources.

CollageOne image is not enough; stack them.

TypographyThe sentence is in the shot.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Natural Born Killers collides broadcast, film, and graphic interruption. Everything Everywhere All at Once lets illustration, stock, and live action share a plane when the universe will not stay one medium.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Mixed media around [Subject], live action, type, illustration, and stock colliding in one plane. Name each medium.

Keep edges visible. Ban a single seamless grade that hides the collision.

Use in Image Generator

Mixed media around [Subject], live action, type, illustration, and stock colliding in one plane.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a graded live-action still with a font on top, or a pure Collage of one photo. The tell is one texture, one grain, one key.

The fix is at least two capture modes, edges showing, one readable subject.

Questions

What is mixed media in film?

Mixed media combines live action with type, illustration, and stock in one plane. No single medium owns the truth of the frame.

Mixed media vs collage

Collage is layers of stills and textures. Mixed media is different capture methods colliding: a photograph next to a drawing next to type. One is torn paper. The other is torn ontology.

When should I use mixed media?

Use it when documents, broadcasts, and bodies cannot be one photograph. Skip it when the scene still wants a single camera's truth.

How do I prompt mixed media for AI image or video?

entries.title: Morphing
entries.text:
Morphing

Geometric image transformation

Morphing cinematography transforms one shape or image continuously into another by interpolating geometry, rather than merely fading between pictures. Identity is a dissolve you can watch as contour.

Volume

Create this Morphing

Narrative function

A face becomes another face while the eyes stay aligned. A body interpolates toward a new contour.

Use it when becoming should be visible as a correspondence of landmarks, not as a cut or a fade. It is the wrong tool when the person stays the same and the room should change, or when makeup and performance can do the work in stages.

If only opacity changes, you shot a dissolve.

How it works

Lock pose, eyeline, and key on two endpoints. Set landmark matches (eyes to eyes, mouth to mouth, silhouette to silhouette).

Separate foreground from background so the warp does not drag the room. Control which features change first.

The midpoint should be an intentional in-between, not a melt. Prompt a morph of the subject into another state: continuous transformation, identity as a dissolve you can watch.

For video, morph into another form over the shot.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when one form must become another in a few seconds of continuous view. Do not use it as a fancy cut between two unrelated shots with no shared landmarks.

Compared with similar shots

Morph as an edit uses the warp as the join between two shots. Morphing here is the geometric interpolation itself.

Transformation can be practical makeup, a set change, or a world swap around a stable body. Morphing is landmark geometry, not a new room.

MorphIdentity is unstable.

TransformationThe change is the scene.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Terminator 2 interpolates chrome and flesh as correspondence. Michael Jackson's Black or White walks faces through aligned landmarks.

Willow interpolates between creature forms. Grammar, not frames to copy.

Willow 1988Transformation passages visibly interpolate between forms.

Prompt it

Morph of [Subject] into another state, continuous transformation, identity as a dissolve you can watch. Video: [Subject] morphs into another form over the shot.

Name both endpoints, keep eyes aligned, and forbid a cross-dissolve of unmatched poses.

Use in Video Generator

Age changes occur gradually and coherently. Use matched endpoint portraits and controlled landmark-based compositing, no identity swap or liquefying face.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dissolve. The tell is two images fading with no shared contour, or a liquefying face with no midpoint design.

The fix is matched pose, matched light, and landmarks that travel.

Questions

What is morphing in film?

Morphing transforms one shape or image continuously into another by interpolating geometry. It is not a fade. Contours travel from one form to the next.

Morphing vs dissolve

A dissolve changes opacity. Morphing changes shape. A cross-dissolve can resemble a morph for a few frames, but it does not continuously transform geometry.

When should I use morphing?

Use it when identity or form must become another form in continuous view, with matched landmarks. Skip it when the room should change around a stable person, or when a simple fade is enough.

How do I prompt morphing for AI image or video?

Write Morph of [Subject] into another state, continuous transformation. Specify both endpoints, aligned eyes, and which features change first. For video, morph over the shot, not a cut.

entries.title: Object Portal
entries.text:
Object Portal

An object portal effect treats a prop as a wormhole: a bag, a screen, or a doorway that should not lead there, opening onto another space. The thing is the cut.

Volume

Create this Object Portal

Narrative function

A filing cabinet leads to a tunnel. A mirror becomes a corridor.

A phone swallows a body. Use it when geography must jump through an object we already believe in as a prop.

It is the wrong tool when the camera itself punches through a wall with no special object, or when a wall is only a screen of light. If matter is optional for the lens, that is a pass-through.

If pictures crawl on architecture, that is a projection.

How it works

Photograph the prop as a real object with thickness, rim, and a key. Composite or project the far space inside its opening.

Parallax the rim against the interior so the hole has depth. The room around the prop stays this world.

Hands, edges, and contact shadows sell the aperture. Prompt an object portal through the subject: a thing opening onto another space, a bag, a screen, a doorway that should not lead there.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a character climbs into a prop and arrives somewhere the room cannot contain. Do not use it as a generic glow around a door that is just a door.

Compared with similar shots

Pass Through travels the camera through architecture as if matter were optional. An object portal needs a prop as the aperture.

Projections put pictures on surfaces. A portal opens onto another space inside the object.

Pass ThroughCut the building, not the film.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

Being John Malkovich sends a body through a small door into a head. The Matrix uses a mirror and other props as passages between worlds.

Grammar for the object as wormhole, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Object portal through [Subject], a thing opening onto another space, a bag, a screen, a doorway that should not lead there. Name the prop, the rim, and the far geography inside it.

Keep the surrounding room in this world.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a glowing doorway or a Pass Through through a wall. The tell is no prop with thickness, or the whole set melting.

The fix is a readable object, a hole with parallax, and two geographies meeting at the rim.

Questions

What is an object portal in film?

An object portal treats a prop as a wormhole. A bag, screen, or doorway opens onto another space that the room should not contain. The object is the cut.

Object portal vs pass through

A pass-through sends the camera through a wall or body as if matter were optional. An object portal requires a thing with a rim: the far world is inside that object.

When should I use object portal?

Use it when a character or look must travel through a prop into another space. Skip it when you only need to fly the camera through architecture.

How do I prompt object portal for AI image or video?

entries.title: Photogrammetry
entries.text:
Photogrammetry

Gravitational lensingSimulation-led imagery

The photogrammetry look reconstructs 3D geometry and texture from overlapping photographs, so a real place is turned into a scanned mesh. Slightly wrong normals, stretched texture, and holes are the evidence of capture.

Volume

Create this Photogrammetry

Narrative function

The camera can orbit a courtyard that was photographed, not built. Faces of stone look photographed because they were, then wrapped onto geometry.

Use it when the scene should feel surveyed: a real site captured as a model. It is the wrong tool for a handmade miniature, and it is not proof of a physics simulation.

A black-hole visualization is simulation-led imagery, a cousin name in the catalog, not a scan.

How it works

Shoot many overlapping stills around the subject, triangulate a mesh, project the photographs as texture. The look: texture stretching at grazing angles, missing undersides, a seam where coverage failed.

Light can be the captured light, or a new CG key on the mesh. The camera path is free because the space is geometry.

Prompt a photogrammetry look: scanned space, slightly wrong mesh, a real place turned into a model.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a real location should be inspectable as a model, slightly too virtual. Do not use it to claim a scientific render is a scan.

Compared with similar shots

Diorama is a built miniature with model lighting. Photogrammetry is photographed reality wrapped on a mesh.

Video Game uses engine lighting and authored assets. The photogrammetry look keeps photo texture and scan error.

DioramaShrink the epic until it fits a shelf.

Video GameThe world is playable.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Experimental documentaries and game cutscenes orbit scanned spaces. Interstellar is listed beside them as simulation-led imagery (Gargantua's computed disk), a cousin of modeled pictures, not a photogrammetric mesh.

Use the scan look for places. Use simulation when the phenomenon was computed.

Interstellar 2014Gargantua and its gravitationally lensed accretion-disk imagery.

Prompt it

Photogrammetry look of [Subject], scanned space, slightly wrong mesh, a real place turned into a model. Name overlapping-photo texture, a hole or stretch, and an orbit or inspection camera.

Ban a toy diorama and ban a perfect game render.

Use in Video Generator

Use a validated ray-traced simulation as the geometric reference and preserve its major contours. Label this as a cinematic visualization, not a newly computed scientific result.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are a Diorama and a clean engine render. The tell is painted miniature charm, or PBR plastic with no photo texture.

The fix is photographic skin on imperfect geometry, seams included.

Questions

What is photogrammetry in film?

Photogrammetry reconstructs 3D geometry and texture from overlapping photographs. The look is a real place turned into a scanned mesh, often with slight error.

Photogrammetry vs diorama

A diorama is built at miniature scale. Photogrammetry starts from photographs of a real site and wraps them on computed geometry. One is a model you light. The other is a survey you inspect.

When should I use photogrammetry?

Use it when a location should read as captured and then modeled, inspectable, slightly wrong. Skip it for handmade miniatures or for computed phenomena that were never photographed.

entries.text:
Ratio Switch

Expanding frameNarrative frame boundary

An aspect ratio switch changes the image's visible boundaries so the container itself widens or closes as the story changes register. The picture is not stretched: previously unseen area is revealed, or the crop tightens.

Volume

Create this Ratio Switch

Narrative function

A square world learns it can become a wide one. A scope picture suddenly sits in a taller box.

The frame is a character. Use it when a period, a freedom, or a constraint should be felt as the edge of the movie.

It is the wrong tool for a zoom, and it is not a mask inside the picture. If the lens merely tightens, the container never changed.

If a keyhole sits inside a stable 16:9, that is masking.

How it works

Compose protected areas for both ratios. Animate the crop or the side mattes.

Preserve subject geometry. Bodies must not squash to fill the new frame.

The camera may be locked. The event is the bounds.

Prompt an aspect-ratio switch on the subject: the frame itself widening or closing. For video, a visible crop or reveal during the sequence.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a character pushes the world open, or when a new time period deserves a different box. Do not use it as a zoom-out that only changes shot size.

Compared with similar shots

Masking cuts a shape inside a stable container. A ratio switch changes the container.

Wide Shot is a shot size inside whatever ratio you already have. Switching ratio is not going wider with the lens.

MaskingShow looking as an object.

Wide ShotDo not isolate yet.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Mommy lets Steve appear to open a constrained frame outward. The Grand Budapest Hotel assigns different narrative periods different frame shapes.

Ozark and other Xavier Dolan films use the same container-as-event grammar. Not frames to copy.

Mommy 2014Steve appears to open the constrained frame outward.

The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014Different narrative periods use different frame shapes.

Prompt it

Aspect-ratio switch on [Subject], the frame itself widening or closing as the story changes register. Video: The frame around [Subject] changes aspect ratio during the sequence, a visible crop or reveal.

Say the image does not stretch. Name the start ratio and the end ratio.

Use in Video Generator

Begin with a young cyclist confined within a square image. As she reaches an open seaside road and takes a deep breath, widen the frame smoothly to a broad rectangle, revealing the ocean on both sides. Reveal previously unseen image area; never stretch her body or bicycle. Animate the framing in post.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are a zoom and a stretch. The tell is the body fattening to fill the new box, or the lens punching in with no matte move.

The fix is a crop or reveal of extra picture, geometry preserved.

Questions

What is a ratio switch in film?

A ratio switch changes the visible boundaries of the image, widening or closing the container. It marks a shift in time, viewpoint, or possibility. The picture is not stretched.

Ratio switch vs masking

Masking puts a shape inside the picture. A ratio switch changes the outer bounds of the movie. One is a hole. The other is a new box.

When should I use a ratio switch?

Use it when the container should act: a period change, a sudden freedom, a learned restriction opening. Skip it when you only need a wider lens or a tighter close-up.

entries.title: Scale Shift
entries.text:
Scale Shift

Dunkirk temporal convergence

Scale shift cinematography changes a body's size against the same room so the figure is suddenly giant or tiny: Alice physics as an optical event. Furniture, shadows, and contact have to match the new ratio.

Volume

Create this Scale Shift

Narrative function

A person stands in a kitchen and the table is a landscape. Or a hand is a building.

The geography did not cut. The scale did.

Use it when relative size is the plot of the shot. The same name is sometimes used for unequal story-time strands, as in Dunkirk's land, sea, and air clocks.

That is editorial scale, not optical size. Do not mix the two tools in one prompt.

How it works

Lock the room plate. Resize the figure with oversized furniture, miniatures, split-scale composites, or a cut that reprints the body at a new height in the same architecture.

Shadows and contact must match the new size: a giant throws a larger shadow from the same key. Forced perspective can help as a static alignment of two real sizes.

Prompt a scale shift of the subject: the body suddenly giant or tiny against the same room.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a person becomes a toy in their own hallway, or a monster in a dollhouse. Do not use it as a simple close-up that only magnifies a detail without changing the body-to-room ratio.

Compared with similar shots

Forced Perspective aligns two real sizes on one focal plane so they look like one scale. Scale shift is the change of that relationship.

Magnification goes closer than a close-up, a world inside a centimeter. It does not make the whole body tiny in the room.

Forced PerspectiveChange size without VFX.

MagnificationGo closer than a close-up.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Honey, I Shrunk the Kids and Ant-Man stage bodies against furniture and grass at the wrong size. Dunkirk and Inception appear in the catalog as temporal-scale cousins: unequal clocks, not Alice rooms.

Use the first pair for optical size. Keep the second pair for editorial time.

Dunkirk 2017Land, sea and air strands span different durations before converging.

Inception 2010Different dream levels unfold at different apparent rates.

Prompt it

Scale shift of [Subject], the body suddenly giant or tiny against the same room, Alice physics. Name the room, the new size, and matching shadows.

Ban a mere close-up and ban stretching the architecture.

Use in Video Generator

Design an intercut rescue story: a mountain team’s six-hour ascent, a driver’s thirty-minute approach and a climber’s final two-minute wait. Build a timeline showing exactly where they converge. Generate separate location strands and edit them toward one shared radio call, not as falsely equal real-time durations.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are a Close-Up and a zoom. The tell is a big face with a normal room, or a lens punch with no furniture scale change.

The fix is the same architecture, a new body-to-room ratio, and contact that fits.

Questions

What is scale shift in film?

A scale shift makes a body giant or tiny against the same room. Relative size changes as an optical event. A separate editorial meaning uses unequal story-time strands.

Scale shift vs forced perspective

Forced perspective is a static alignment of two real sizes so they read as one scale. Scale shift is the change: the body becomes the wrong size in a room we already know.

When should I use scale shift?

Use it when size is the joke or the threat inside a known space. Skip it when you only need a closer lens, and do not confuse it with intercutting unequal clocks.

How do I prompt scale shift for AI image or video?

Write Scale shift of [Subject], the body suddenly giant or tiny against the same room. Keep the architecture, match the shadows, and name the new size.

entries.title: Shadow Box
entries.text:
Shadow Box

Shadow-box cinematography tells the story in layered cut-outs, depth as stacked silhouettes, a diorama of darkness. Figures are unfilled, and distance is paper stacked in front of a hard backlight.

Volume

Create this Shadow Box

Narrative function

A procession of blacks: a rider, a tree, a palace, each on its own plane. Use it when the scene should be read as theatre cut from card, not as a modeled room with fill.

It is the wrong tool for a single backlit person in a real location, and for a miniature that still has painted faces. If there is only one plane of black, you shot a silhouette.

If the model is fully dressed and scaled, you shot a diorama.

How it works

Cut figures and architecture as separate layers. Space them in depth in front of a hard source.

No fill on the faces. Edges stay graphic.

Parallax between layers if the camera creeps. The source is behind.

The camera is in front. Color, if any, is in the backlight or in a few tinted planes, not in modeled skin.

Prompt a shadow-box of the subject: layered cut-outs, depth as stacked silhouettes, a diorama of darkness.

When to use it

Use it for the beat that should feel like a night play made of paper. Do not use it when the face must carry skin and eye light.

Compared with similar shots

Silhouette is one backlit figure, usually in real space. A shadow box stacks many cut-outs.

Diorama is a miniature world with modeled volume. A shadow box is layers of black, not a tiny set with fill.

SilhouetteIdentity is less important than shape.

DioramaShrink the epic until it fits a shelf.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Adventures of Prince Achmed is silhouette animation as stacked theatre. Kara Walker's language of cut-out processions is the still and installation cousin.

Grammar of layered black, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Shadow-box of [Subject], layered cut-outs, depth as stacked silhouettes, a diorama of darkness. Name several planes, a hard backlight, and no fill on the figures.

Ban painted faces and ban a single silhouette in a real street.

Use in Image Generator

Shadow-box of [Subject], layered cut-outs, depth as stacked silhouettes, a diorama of darkness.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are a lone Silhouette and a lit Diorama. The tell is skin texture, or only one black plane.

The fix is stacked cut-outs, hard source behind, unfilled figures.

Questions

What is a shadow box in film?

A shadow box tells the story in layered cut-outs. Depth is stacked silhouettes, like a diorama of darkness, not a filled naturalistic space.

Shadow box vs silhouette

A silhouette is usually one backlit body. A shadow box is many cut-out planes stacked in depth. One is a figure. The other is paper theatre.

When should I use a shadow box?

Use it when the scene should be read as stacked blacks: a procession, a fable, a night cut from card. Skip it when the face needs skin and a key.

How do I prompt a shadow box for AI image or video?

Write Shadow-box of [Subject], layered cut-outs, depth as stacked silhouettes. Demand several planes, a hard backlight, and unfilled figures.
