entries.title: Transformation
entries.text:
Transformation

Psychological background transformationSubject-stable world change

Transformation cinematography makes a body, room, or object become something else in continuous view. The camera keeps watching while the state changes, with a stable anchor so the becoming can be read.

Volume

Create this Transformation

Narrative function

A kiss turns the restaurant into a memory. A man becomes an animal in stages.

A liquid takes a face. Use it when the audience should not be allowed a cut to skip the becoming.

It is the wrong tool when you only need a landmark warp of one contour into another, or when a new scene should simply start. If the job is matched geometry between two portraits, morphing is cleaner.

If both body and world melt at random, the anchor is gone.

How it works

Decide what stays. A subject-stable world change matches pose, contact, and key while the background is exchanged by a move, an occlusion, a projection, a set change, or a tracked composite.

A body transformation stages makeup, puppet, or digital change in order, with weight and effort. Light the new state with a source that still makes sense on the skin.

Prompt a transformation of the subject: a body, room, or object becoming something else in continuous view.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when becoming is the action: a memory room, a creature, a substance taking form. Do not use it as a morph between two unmatched stills.

Compared with similar shots

Morphing interpolates landmarks from one contour to another. Transformation can be practical, architectural, or a world swap around a stable person.

Morph uses the warp as an edit join. Creature stages (werewolf cinema) are performance and makeup, not only a warp.

MorphingBecoming is visible.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

Anamorphic FlareNight lights and headlights should write on the lens.

In film

Vertigo's revolving kiss shifts the surrounding setting toward memory. Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind lets memory spaces change around the couple.

An American Werewolf in London and The Fly stage the body as a visible change of state. Terminator 2 and The Abyss sit nearby as shape that reforms.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Vertigo 1958The revolving kiss shifts the surrounding setting toward Scottie’s memory.

Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind 2004Memory spaces change or lose continuity around the characters.

Terminator 2: Judgment Day 1991The T-1000 changes shape and reforms within scenes.

The Abyss 1989The water pseudopod takes on a face.

Prompt it

Transformation of [Subject], a body, room, or object becoming something else in continuous view. Video: [Subject] transforms across the shot, a visible change of state.

Name what stays (pose, face, contact) and what changes (room, species, substance).

Use in Video Generator

Orbit slowly around two fictional former friends embracing in a modern station. Keep their bodies and contact continuous while the architecture behind them gradually becomes the childhood railway platform they remember. Change only the surrounding world, with coherent light and perspective. Plan matched environment plates and composite the transition; no melting faces.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a generic morph of everything. The tell is melting faces and melting walls at once, no anchor.

The fix is a stable perceptual center and a designed change of state.

Questions

What is transformation in film?

Transformation makes a body, room, or object become something else in continuous view. The change is the scene, not a cut to a new state.

Transformation vs morphing

Morphing is geometric interpolation between matched forms. Transformation is a change of state that can be makeup, a walking set, or a world exchanged around a stable subject. One is landmarks. The other is becoming.

When should I use transformation?

Use it when the audience must watch the becoming: memory rooms, creature stages, a substance taking a face. Skip it for a simple fade or an unmatched morph.

How do I prompt transformation for AI image or video?

Write Transformation of [Subject], a body, room, or object becoming something else in continuous view. Name the anchor and the new state. For video, transform across the shot.

entries.title: Typography
entries.text:
Typography

Narrative main titlesGraphic opening sequence

Kinetic typography puts words in the world of the shot as objects: titles that occupy space, letters with scale, parallax, and a surface. The sentence is in the picture, not parked as a caption.

Volume

Create this Typography

Narrative function

A name walks the street. A credit is scratched into a notebook.

Type pursues a figure. Use it when the film should teach its pattern before or during the action, and when letters are part of the blocking.

It is the wrong tool for a lower-third, and a single handsome card is not yet a title sequence. If live action, drawing, and stock collide as equal media, you are in mixed media.

If paper layers tear without readable words as objects, you are in collage.

How it works

Choose one visual rule: ink that becomes a map, letters that stand in the set, type that tracks a body. Light in-world letters as surfaces (a key, an edge).

Reserve space for exact spelling. Animate progression before dropping credits.

The camera can dolly so type parallax against walls. Prompt typography in the world of the subject: words as objects, titles that occupy space, kinetic type.

When to use it

Use it for the beat when a word must share space with a person, or when an opening must tell a miniature story in letters. Do not use it as unreadable scribble over a portrait.

Compared with similar shots

Mixed Media collides several capture modes. Typography can live inside a single photographed world.

Collage layers images. Type may appear there, but collage does not require words as blocking.

Mixed MediaNo single medium owns the truth.

CollageOne image is not enough; stack them.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Vertigo's spiral opening sets a pattern of obsession in letter and shape. Se7en builds credits from hands, notebooks, and material type.

Catch Me If You Can condenses pursuit into animated letterforms. Annie Hall and Scott Pilgrim vs.

the World put sentences into the scene. Grammar, not frames to copy.

Vertigo 1958The spiral-based opening establishes a pattern of obsession and instability.

Se7en 1995Hands, notebooks and material fragments construct a disturbing preparatory ritual.

Catch Me If You Can 2002Animated pursuit imagery condenses the film’s identity game.

Annie Hall 1977Subtitles expose thoughts that differ from the spoken rooftop conversation.

Scott Pilgrim vs. the World 2010Words and graphic marks become part of the film’s expressive action.

Prompt it

Typography in the world of [Subject], words as objects, titles that occupy space, kinetic type. Name the words, the surface they sit on, and the light.

Ban decorative gibberish and ban a floating caption with no place in the room.

Use in Video Generator

Design a forty-second title sequence for a film about a missing cartographer. A single ink line becomes a street, a fingerprint ridge and a coastline before vanishing at the edge of a map. Generate visual elements separately; animate the transformations and add exact credits in a motion-graphics timeline. No arbitrary stock-footage montage.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a title card or a caption. The tell is unreadable AI lettering, or type glued to the frame with no space in the set.

The fix is exact words, a surface, and a rule that progresses.

Questions

What is typography in film?

Typography here is kinetic type in the world of the shot: words as objects, titles that occupy space. A sentence lives in the picture rather than as a caption.

Typography vs mixed media

Mixed media collides live action, drawing, type, and stock. Typography can be letters inside one photographed space. The letters are the event, not one of several crashing media.

When should I use typography?

Use it when words must occupy the scene or when an opening needs a miniature story in letters. Skip it for a simple name card or unreadable overlay.

How do I prompt typography for AI image or video?

entries.title: Wigglegram
entries.text:
Wigglegram

A wigglegram is a short stereo shiver: two or three frames rocking so depth reads as a fidget. The viewpoints are a few centimeters apart, so depth is a twitch, not a dolly.

Volume

Create this Wigglegram

Narrative function

A postcard comes alive as a cheap lenticular. The subject stays almost still.

The room jumps between two eyes. Use it when you want stereo without a move, a GIF of depth.

It is the wrong tool for a real tracking shot, and it is not camera shake. If planes peel continuously, you have parallax from travel.

If the same viewpoint chatters, you have a wiggle or a stutter.

How it works

Lock two (or three) stills on a stereo baseline of a few centimeters, same height, same lens. Flicker A-B-A.

Foreground shifts more than the back, which is the disparity. No motion blur from a pan.

Light both frames with the same key so only position changes. Prompt a wigglegram of the subject: two or three frames rocking, a cheap stereo shiver.

For video, a short wiggle between two viewpoints.

When to use it

Use it for the beat that should feel like a lenticular or a stereo GIF: a portrait, a product, a joke of depth. Do not use it in place of a dolly through a room.

Compared with similar shots

Parallax comes from the camera traveling so planes peel at different speeds. A wigglegram only rocks between two locked viewpoints.

Stutter / Stop-Stutter is a temporal step of one take. Wiggle is a tiny tremor of the support, not a stereo pair.

ParallaxProve the world has layers.

Stutter / Stop-StutterThe mind skips.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

Lenticular photos and GIF stereo are the well-known uses: postcards, early web 3D fidgets, social stereo stills. Cinema borrows that twitch.

Grammar of two eyes, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Wigglegram of [Subject], two or three frames rocking, a cheap stereo shiver, depth as a fidget. Video: A short wiggle between two viewpoints of [Subject], stereoscopic shiver.

Name a small baseline and a locked subject. Ban a dolly and ban handheld shake.

Use in Video Generator

A short wiggle between two viewpoints of [Subject], stereoscopic shiver.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are Wiggle shake and a mini Dolly In. The tell is blur from motion, or a continuous path.

The fix is two sharp stills a few centimeters apart, flickering.

Questions

What is wigglegram in film?

A wigglegram rocks two or three frames from slightly different viewpoints so depth reads as a stereo shiver. It is a fidget of disparity, not a camera move.

Wigglegram vs parallax

Parallax is continuous relative motion of planes as the camera travels. A wigglegram is a short loop between two locked stereo stills. One is a path. The other is a twitch.

When should I use a wigglegram?

Use it when depth should feel like a lenticular postcard or a stereo GIF. Skip it when the scene needs a real tracking shot.

How do I prompt wigglegram for AI image or video?

Write Wigglegram of [Subject], two or three frames rocking, a cheap stereo shiver. For video, a short wiggle between two viewpoints. Keep the subject still and the baseline small.

entries.title: X-Ray
entries.text:
X-Ray

X-ray cinematography images through a surface as if denser structure were visible: bones, wiring, a body as diagram. Transmission, not reflectance, is the physics.

Create this X-Ray

Narrative function

Skin becomes a veil. The interior is the subject.

Use it when the story needs to see through: a medical look, a machine's vision, a suitcase, a chest. It is the wrong tool for heat, and for foliage that glows in near-infrared.

If warmth is false color, you want thermal. If leaves go pale and skies go dark, you want infrared.

How it works

Render or photograph as transmission: denser parts (bone, metal) hold more of the beam and read as structure. Invert or not, but keep a graphic interior with little surface makeup.

A hard, even backlight through the subject helps. Keep one body readable as a diagram, not a smear of glow.

Prompt an x-ray view of the subject: interior structure, bones or wiring, a body as diagram.

When to use it

Use it for the beat of seeing through a person, a wall, or a device. Do not use it as a teal grade on ordinary skin.

Compared with similar shots

Thermal maps heat as false color. Infrared is near-IR reflectance, often odd foliage and skin, not a skeleton.

X-ray is transmission through the object, structure as diagram.

ThermalSee temperature, not light.

InfraredThe world should look like another planet that is still Earth.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Abyss HUD and science films treat seeing-through as a device overlay or a laboratory plate. Superhero x-ray vision is the pop grammar of the same diagram.

Uses of interior structure, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

X-ray view of [Subject], interior structure, bones or wiring, a body as diagram. Demand transmission, a readable skeleton or circuit, and no thermal palette.

Ban glowing skin that is only a grade.

Use in Image Generator

X-ray view of [Subject], interior structure, bones or wiring, a body as diagram.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are Thermal and a ghostly double exposure. The tell is heat colors, or a transparent person with a normal room and no structure.

The fix is bones or wiring as the picture, graphic, transmitted.

Questions

What is x-ray in film?

An x-ray look images through surfaces so interior structure, bones, or wiring become the picture. It is a diagram of density, not a photograph of skin.

X-ray vs thermal

Thermal shows heat. X-ray shows transmission through matter. One is temperature as color. The other is structure as a plate.

When should I use x-ray?

Use it when the story must see through a body, a wall, or a machine. Skip it for night hunts (thermal) or for IR foliage looks.

How do I prompt x-ray for AI image or video?

Write X-ray view of [Subject], interior structure, bones or wiring, a body as diagram. Specify transmission and a readable interior. Do not ask for heat colors.

entries.title: Zoetrope
entries.text:
Zoetrope

Zoetrope cinematography shows the frames inside a movement: stroboscopic slices of a spinning action, motion as a drum of poses. You see the sampling, not a smooth blur.

Volume

Create this Zoetrope

Narrative function

A horse's legs become a ring of stills. A spinning body is a drum of slices.

Use it when the point is that motion is made of frames, a toy of persistence of vision on screen. It is the wrong tool for ordinary slow motion, and for stop-motion of a puppet that never spins.

If you repeat frames of a continuous take to stutter time, that is step-printing. If an object is posed per frame on a table, that is stop-motion.

How it works

Strobe the action, or present discrete poses around a rotation, like slits in a drum. Each slice is sharp.

The gaps are the point. A hard, brief source (strobe, shuttered light) freezes each pose.

The camera can be locked on the drum or on a repeating run. Prompt a zoetrope of the subject: stroboscopic slices of a spinning action, motion as a drum of frames.

For video, stroboscopic zoetrope slices in repeating action.

When to use it

Use it for the beat that should look like a Victorian motion toy, or a spin sampled into poses. Do not use it as a generic choppy grade on a walk that is not a drum of frames.

Compared with similar shots

Stop Motion poses an object once per frame. A zoetrope samples a spin or a repeating action as a ring of slices.

Step Printing repeats frames of a photographed take to slow or stutter it. The zoetrope shows the drum.

Stop MotionMotion should feel made.

Step PrintingLonging that cannot move at normal speed.

Lens FlareLight is too strong to be polite.

In film

The Horse in Motion is the scientific ancestor: sampled gait as a sequence of stills. Batman Begins uses zoetrope imagery as a motion toy inside the story.

Grammar of sampled spin, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Zoetrope of [Subject], stroboscopic slices of a spinning action, motion as a drum of frames. Video: Stroboscopic zoetrope slices of [Subject] in repeating action.

Demand discrete sharp poses, a spin or cycle, and visible sampling. Ban smooth blur.

Use in Video Generator

Stroboscopic zoetrope slices of [Subject] in repeating action.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousins are Slow Motion and Stutter / Stop-Stutter. The tell is a fluid overcrank, or a walk that hitch-steps without a drum of slices.

The fix is strobe-sharp poses around a repeating spin.

Questions

What is zoetrope in film?

A zoetrope treatment shows the frames inside a movement, like stroboscopic slices of a spinning action. Motion reads as a drum of poses.

Zoetrope vs stop motion

Stop-motion animates an object pose by pose. A zoetrope samples a spinning or repeating action as slits of frames. One is a puppet on a table. The other is a drum of slices.

When should I use zoetrope?

Use it when you want the audience to see sampling: a spin, a gait, a Victorian motion toy. Skip it as a random choppy look on ordinary coverage.

How do I prompt zoetrope for AI image or video?

Write Zoetrope of [Subject], stroboscopic slices of a spinning action, motion as a drum of frames. For video, repeating strobe slices. Keep each pose sharp.

entries.title: Focus Change
entries.text:
Focus Change

Focus change cinematography jumps or slides the plane of sharpness to a new fact, a rack without apology. The mid-blur is short, and the new plane owns the shot as soon as it lands.

Volume

Create this Focus Change

Narrative function

A glass goes soft. A face snaps true.

Attention relocates. Use it when the point is the new owner of the frame, not the poetry of traveling blur.

Keep downward travel. Delay gravity on hair, coat, and debris more than on the torso.

entries.text:
Smash and Grab

Edges barrel. Keep one catchlight.

entries.title: Particles
entries.text:
Particles

Particle effects cinematography fills the air with countable bits: dust, sparks, pollen, a weather of motes, each one catching light. Atmosphere you can inventory, not a blanket of fog.

If the picture is only the beam, you want volumetric light. If the bits are only dust in a church, dust motes may be enough.

How it works

Backlight the bits. Place a hard source so each mote has a specular tick.

Name the species: dust, embers, pollen, ash. Keep the subject readable through the cloud.

Volume is a shaft, not a filter over the whole frame. The camera can be locked.

Count the eyes. Place them as objects: on skin, on walls, as a field of viewpoints around a still center.

Keep a readable subject so the swarm has a king. Light each iris with a small catchlight if they are organs.
